definition.name: aihot__aihot_get_latest_f4723743
definition.title: Latest AI news
definition.description: Get the latest AIHOT items for a 24-hour or 7-day briefing. Prefer selected mode unless the user explicitly asks for every public item. Do not use this for named-topic search or multi-source event context.

window.description: Time window. Use 24h for a current briefing and 7d for a weekly view.

mode.description: selected returns editorial picks; all returns every public item.

category.description: Optional category: ai-models, ai-products, industry, paper, tip, opinion.

limit.description: Maximum number of results, from 1 to 30.

definition.name: aihot__aihot_search_2b62aad8
definition.title: Search AI news
definition.description: Search AIHOT's latest 7 days by a 2–200 character topic, company, model, product, or person. It searches editorial picks first and automatically expands to all public items only when picks have no result.

window.description: Search window. Defaults to the latest 7 days.

category.description: Optional category: ai-models, ai-products, industry, paper, tip, opinion.

limit.description: Maximum number of results, from 1 to 30.

definition.name: aihot__aihot_get_hot_topics_8d75c048
definition.title: Hot topics
definition.description: Get the current AIHOT Top 10 with each event's one-based rank. Use this for 'what is hot now' and to discover valid story public IDs (the last path segment of each event's timeline link); use aihot_get_latest for a chronological news list.

limit.description: Maximum number of current topics, from 1 to 10.

definition.name: aihot__aihot_get_story_83c08cef
definition.title: Story timeline
definition.description: Get the evolving timeline, latest development, AI digest, and related events for one public story. Only pass a public_id obtained from aihot_get_hot_topics; never invent or infer IDs.

public_id.description: Opaque story public ID from aihot_get_hot_topics; never guess it.

report_limit.description: Maximum number of timeline reports, from 1 to 50.

definition.name: aihot__aihot_get_daily_61d633a5
definition.title: Daily report
definition.description: Get AIHOT's edited daily overview, either the latest issue or a real YYYY-MM-DD date. Use this when the user asks for a daily report rather than a raw chronological list.

date.description: Optional date in YYYY-MM-DD. Omit for the latest daily report.

definition.name: aihot__aihot_get_weekly_a95382e2
definition.title: Weekly report
definition.description: Get AIHOT's edited weekly report: the week's most important events chosen from its dailies, grouped by section, with an overview. Omit week for the latest.

week.description: Optional ISO week such as 2026-W39. Omit for the latest weekly report.

definition.name: aihot__aihot_get_monthly_996a8f15
definition.title: Monthly report
definition.description: Get AIHOT's edited monthly report: the month's most important events chosen from its dailies, grouped by section, with an overview. Omit month for the latest.

month.description: Optional month in YYYY-MM such as 2026-09. Omit for the latest monthly report.

definition.name: aihot__aihot_get_codex_resets_ad28548d
definition.title: Codex quota resets
definition.description: Get AIHOT's monitor of OpenAI Codex quota resets and reset-card announcements: the latest check, recent resets and the full calendar link.

definition.name: leis__search_c71f8773
definition.title: Buscar normas (formato OpenAI)
definition.description: Busca normas da legislação brasileira por palavras-chave, número e ano (ex.: 'código de defesa do consumidor', 'lei 8078 1990', 'decreto 11.000'). Cobre por padrão a Constituição e normas federais; uma sigla de UF em maiúsculas na consulta (ex.: 'ICMS SP') muda a busca para a legislação daquele estado, e termos como 'súmula', 'ANVISA' ou 'tratado' ativam as respectivas esferas. Para filtros completos use buscar_normas. Retorna JSON {results:[{id,title,url}]}; o id é o caminho da norma, usado em fetch.

query.description: Consulta em linguagem natural ou número da norma

definition.name: leis__fetch_f2ccbe53

definition.description: Retorna o texto integral de uma norma pelo id (caminho retornado por search, ex.: 'federal/leis-ordinarias/1990/lei-8078.md'). Retorna JSON {id,title,text,url,metadata}. Textos muito longos são truncados — use ler_norma para paginar ou ler um artigo.

id.description: Caminho da norma no acervo

definition.name: leis__buscar_normas_6cd648c2
definition.title: Buscar normas
definition.description: Busca no índice da legislação brasileira (título, tipo, número, data e ementa). Todas as palavras precisam aparecer (prefixo de palavra, sem acento/caixa); números casam com o número da norma e anos com a data. Sem filtros a busca cobre Constituição + federal. Use 'uf' para legislação estadual/municipal de um estado, 'esfera' para reguladores, jurisprudência, tratados etc. Normas revogadas são omitidas por padrão.

consulta.description: Palavras-chave e/ou número, ex.: 'licitações contratos', 'lei 14133', 'ICMS substituição tributária'

esfera.description: Esferas a pesquisar. Padrão: constituicao+federal (ou estadual+municipal quando 'uf' é informado)

uf.description: Sigla do estado (ex.: SP, RJ, DF)

tipo.description: Tipo de norma, ex.: 'Lei Complementar', 'Decreto', 'Emenda Constitucional', 'Súmula', 'Resolução'

colecao.description: Prefixo de coleção (pasta) do acervo, ex.: 'federal/leis-complementares', 'reguladores/anvisa'. Veja listar_colecoes

definition.name: leis__ler_norma_43a1190f

artigo.description: Número do artigo a extrair, ex.: '5', '5º', '121-A'

termo.description: Termo a procurar quando não se informa artigo

definition.name: pubmed__pubmed_search_articles_63a080f0
definition.title: Pubmed Search Articles
definition.description: Search PubMed with full query syntax, filters, and date ranges. Returns PMIDs and optional brief summaries. Supports field-specific filters (author, journal, MeSH terms), common filters (language, species, free full text), and pagination via offset for paging through large result sets.

query.description: PubMed search query (supports full NCBI syntax), sent as written apart from inline formatting tags such as `<i>`, which are removed. Omit it or pass an empty string to search on the filters alone, which needs `author`, `journal`, `meshTerms`, or `publicationTypes`; `all[sb]` selects the whole database for a slice by the other filters. A query given must carry a search term: a value that is blank once markup, bracketed field tags (`[pdat]`), parentheses, and invisible characters such as a zero-width space are disregarded is rejected rather than sent to PubMed.

maxResults.description: Maximum results to return, up to 1000 per call; a larger value returns 1000 with a notice naming the next `offset`. 0 returns only `totalCount`.

offset.description: Result offset for pagination (0-based). PubMed serves at most the first 9999 records of a result set, so this caps at 9998; narrow the query or add filters to reach anything beyond it.

sort.description: Sort order: relevance (default), pub_date (newest first), author, or journal

dateRange.description: Filter by date range. The filter is applied only when both `minDate` and `maxDate` are non-empty; either one empty disables the entire date range. A partial date covers its whole year or month, and a range whose `minDate` falls after its `maxDate` is rejected: `2024/06` to `2024` is valid, `2024/07` to `2024/06/30` is not.

minDate.description: Start date (YYYY/MM/DD, YYYY/MM, or YYYY). Must be a real calendar date — `2023/02/29` is rejected. Leaving it empty drops the whole date range, not just this bound; for no lower bound pass a wide sentinel such as `1000`.

maxDate.description: End date (YYYY/MM/DD, YYYY/MM, or YYYY). Must be a real calendar date — `2023/02/29` is rejected. Leaving it empty drops the whole date range, not just this bound; for no upper bound pass a wide sentinel such as `3000`.

publicationTypes.description: Filter by publication type (e.g. "Review", "Clinical Trial", "Meta-Analysis"). Multiple values are OR'd — any match qualifies. Empty strings are skipped; an element of only whitespace, invisible characters, markup, parentheses, brackets, or double quotes is rejected.

author.description: Filter by author name (e.g. "Smith J"). An empty string applies no filter; a value of only whitespace, invisible characters, markup, parentheses, brackets, or double quotes is rejected.

journal.description: Filter by journal name. An empty string applies no filter; a value of only whitespace, invisible characters, markup, parentheses, brackets, or double quotes is rejected.

meshTerms.description: Filter by MeSH terms. Multiple terms are AND'd — all must match. Empty strings are skipped; an element of only whitespace, invisible characters, markup, parentheses, brackets, or double quotes is rejected.

language.description: Filter by language (e.g. "english"). An empty string applies no filter; a value of only whitespace, invisible characters, markup, parentheses, brackets, or double quotes is rejected.

freeFullText.description: Only include free full text articles

species.description: Filter by species: `humans` adds `humans[MeSH Terms]`, `animals` adds `"animals"[mh:noexp]` (animals other than humans; a record indexed for both stays in). Both match only records with MEDLINE species indexing, which preprints and ahead-of-print citations lack.

summaryCount.description: Fetch brief summaries for the top N results (0 = PMIDs only), up to 50 per call; a larger value fetches 50 with a notice. Pass the PMIDs past the cap to pubmed_fetch_articles.

query.description: Original query; empty when the search ran on the filters alone

offset.description: Result offset used

authors.description: Formatted author string — the first three of the record's own authors, then "et al.". On an NCBI Bookshelf chapter these are the chapter's authors; the book's editors are reported separately in `editors`.

source.description: Journal the article appeared in. Absent on an NCBI Bookshelf record, which has no journal — its venue is in `bookTitle` and `publisherName` instead, and `docType` says which kind of record it is.

bookTitle.description: Title of the book an NCBI Bookshelf record belongs to, e.g. "GeneReviews(®)". Present instead of `source` on a book record; absent on a journal article.

publisherName.description: Publisher of the book an NCBI Bookshelf record belongs to. Present only on a book record; absent on a journal article.

docType.description: What PubMed classifies this record as: "chapter" or "book" for an NCBI Bookshelf record, "citation" for an ordinary journal article. Absent when PubMed supplies none.

editors.description: Editors of the containing book, kept out of `authors` so they cannot displace the record's own authors. Absent on a journal article and on a book that credits no editors.

items.description: One editor, "Surname Initials" as ESummary renders it

pubDate.description: Publication date as YYYY-MM-DD; a month- or year-only date reads as the first day of that month or year. On an NCBI Bookshelf chapter (`docType` "chapter") it is the chapter's own date — its last revision, otherwise its contribution — not the year its book began.

doi.description: DOI, cased as NCBI reports it. DOIs are case-insensitive by spec and no case normalization is applied here, so casing can differ from a Europe PMC-sourced `doi` — compare the two case-insensitively.

items.description: Brief article summary

summaries.description: Brief summaries (empty array when summaryCount is 0)

effectiveQuery.description: The term sent to PubMed: the query as written, with a clause appended for each active filter, or the filter clauses alone, joined by AND, when no query was given. Only inline formatting tags with no attributes (`<i>`, `<b>`, `<em>`, `<strong>`, `<u>` and their closers) are removed; `&`, `<`, and `>` are sent as written.

dateRange.description: Date range filter applied to the search

dateType.description: Applied date field used for the range filter

publicationTypes.description: Publication type filters applied to the search

author.description: Author filter applied to the search

journal.description: Journal filter applied to the search

meshTerms.description: MeSH term filters applied to the search

language.description: Language filter applied to the search

hasAbstract.description: Whether results were restricted to articles with abstracts

freeFullText.description: Whether results were restricted to free full-text articles

species.description: Species filter applied to the search: `humans` as `humans[MeSH Terms]`, `animals` as `"animals"[mh:noexp]`

appliedFilters.description: Filter values applied to the PubMed query, as sent: each text value as written, formatting tags removed, and dates in YYYY/MM/DD form

notice.description: Optional guidance when the result set does not reflect what was asked for — a field tag PubMed ignored, a phrase it matched nothing for, a dateRange dropped for having one bound, no matches at all, paging past the end, or a `maxResults` or `summaryCount` past its per-call cap, served at the cap. Absent when nothing applies.

error.description: Present when the call failed. Absent on success.

code.description: JSON-RPC error code for this failure.

message.description: Human-readable description of what went wrong.

reason.description: Machine-readable failure mode. Declared by this tool: `queue_full`: The local NCBI request queue shed the call — the queue is full, or the call cannot start before its total deadline (for example behind the cooldown that follows an NCBI 429). `ncbi_unreachable`: NCBI E-utilities failed on every attempt the retry budget allowed — retries ran out, or the next backoff would overrun the total deadline. `ncbi_rate_limited`: NCBI answered HTTP 429 (too many requests) and the call stopped on it — retries ran out, the next backoff would overrun the total deadline, or the Retry-After NCBI named outlasts the time left or the 30-second backoff cap. `ncbi_deadline_exceeded`: The total NCBI request deadline expired before NCBI answered successfully — mid-request, while queued, or during a retry backoff. `ncbi_invalid_response`: NCBI returned a body that could not be parsed (invalid XML/JSON). `ncbi_resource_not_found`: NCBI returned a structured "not found" error for the requested ID(s). `blank_query`: The query contains no search term: nothing is left once whitespace and invisible characters such as a zero-width space are disregarded. pubmed_search_articles and pubmed_europepmc_search first decode HTML entities and also disregard markup and parentheses, so `()`, ``, and ` ` hold no term there; pubmed_search_articles also disregards bracketed field tags such as `[pdat]`. On pubmed_search_articles an exactly-empty `query` is not blank: it means no query, and the search runs on its filters. `invalid_date_range`: A `dateRange` bound is not a real calendar date — a month outside 01–12, day 00, or a day past the end of its month such as `2023/02/29` — or `minDate` falls after `maxDate` once PubMed expands each partial date: `minDate` from the start of its year or month, `maxDate` to the end. `blank_filter`: An `author`, `journal`, or `language` value, or a `publicationTypes` or `meshTerms` element, holds no term once markup is removed and HTML entities are decoded — only whitespace, invisible characters such as a zero-width space, parentheses, brackets, or double quotes are left, as in `()` or `""` — so its field clause would carry no term. An exactly-empty string is not blank here; it sets no filter. `no_search_term`: No `query` is given — it is omitted or an empty string — and no subject filter (`author`, `journal`, `meshTerms`, or `publicationTypes`) carries a term. `dateRange`, `language`, `species`, `hasAbstract`, and `freeFullText` narrow a search without saying what it is for, so they cannot run one alone. Other values are possible when a failure originates below the handler.

recovery.description: Actionable next step for the caller.

definition.name: pubmed__pubmed_fetch_articles_2c8cc296
definition.title: Pubmed Fetch Articles
definition.description: Fetch full article metadata by PubMed IDs. Returns detailed article information including abstract, authors, journal, MeSH terms, linked retraction, erratum, and comment notices, and databank accessions such as trial registration IDs; grants and the members of a collective author are opt-in (`includeGrants`, `includeInvestigators`). Set `maxResponseCharacters` to bound the whole response: articles past the ceiling are deferred whole and listed in `deferred.ids` for a follow-up call.

includeInvestigators.description: Include `investigators`: the members NCBI lists for a collective author such as "TGU Investigators". Off by default because the list is unbounded: consortium trials name thousands, at about 60 characters of JSON each — PMID 33933206 lists 6,349, adding about 372,000 characters to its record. Under `maxResponseCharacters` they count toward the size of their article, which is deferred whole when it no longer fits.

maxResponseCharacters.description: Opt-in ceiling for the whole response, in characters. Each article is measured as the JSON record it is returned as — title, abstract, authors, journal, MeSH terms, grants, identifiers, every field it carries. Articles are kept in response order until the next one would cross the ceiling; that article and the rest are deferred whole (never partially populated) and listed in `deferred.ids`. Response envelope fields — counts, `unavailablePmids`, `deferred` itself — are not counted. Omit to return every resolved article.

recordType.description: Which kind of PubMed record this is, set from the XML element it arrived in: `journal-article` for an ordinary article, `book-chapter` for an NCBI Bookshelf chapter, `book` for a whole Bookshelf book. Read this to tell the three apart — `publicationTypes` cannot, because PubMed labels a Bookshelf record "Review" or "Study Guide". `journalInfo` is present only on `journal-article`; `book` only on the other two.

title.description: Article title — the chapter title on a `book-chapter`, and the book title on a `book` record, where it repeats `book.title`.

affiliations.description: Deduplicated affiliations, referenced by `affiliationIndices`: the authors' entries first, then any that only `investigators` carry

authors.description: Author list. On a `book-chapter` these are the chapter's own authors, never the book's editors, which are in `book.editors`. Empty on a Bookshelf record that credits neither.

suffix.description: Generational name suffix verbatim from NCBI `Suffix` (e.g. "Jr", "2nd", "3rd"), never normalized. Absent when NCBI gives none.

collectiveName.description: Group/collective author name. NCBI may list the members of the group separately; set `includeInvestigators` to return them as `investigators`.

affiliationIndices.description: Indices into the top-level affiliations array

items.description: Author record

investigators.description: Members of the article's collective author, from NCBI's `InvestigatorList`: every list flattened in NCBI's order, uncapped. They are not authors, and no citation style lists them. Present only when `includeInvestigators` is set and the record lists any; never on `book-chapter` or `book` records.

suffix.description: Generational name suffix verbatim from NCBI `Suffix` (e.g. "Jr", "2nd"). Absent when NCBI gives none.

affiliationIndices.description: Indices into the top-level affiliations array, where an investigator's affiliations follow the authors'

items.description: One member of a collective author, from NCBI's `InvestigatorList`

elocationId.description: Electronic article locator from NCBI `ELocationID` — the publisher-assigned article number (e.g. "2400512"). Journals that assign article numbers instead of pages often omit pagination entirely, leaving this the only locator. Never a substitute for `pages`, and never the DOI: a DOI-typed `ELocationID` is reported in `doi` instead. Absent when the only locator NCBI supplies is marked invalid.

elocationIdType.description: Type of `elocationId`, from NCBI's `EIdType` attribute — "pii" in practice. Free-form: NCBI does not close the set, so treat an unfamiliar value as opaque.

journalInfo.description: Journal information. Present on `journal-article` records only — absent on `book-chapter` and `book` records, because a Bookshelf record has no journal and its book title is never reported as one; read `book` for those. (#114)

title.description: Title of the containing book, from `Book/BookTitle` (e.g. "GeneReviews®"). On a `book` record this is the same value as the record's own `title`.

publisherLocation.description: Place of publication, from `Book/Publisher/PublisherLocation` (e.g. "Seattle (WA)"). Absent when NCBI supplies no place.

pubDate.description: Publication year from `Book/PubDate`. Year only — NCBI's month and day are not reported, since no citation style uses them for a book.

beginningDate.description: First year of a continuously-updated book, from `Book/BeginningDate` (GeneReviews runs from 1993). Absent on a book published once.

endingDate.description: Last year of a closed date range, from `Book/EndingDate`. Absent while a book is still being updated, which leaves the range open-ended.

medium.description: Medium the book is published in, from `Book/Medium` — "Internet" wherever NCBI supplies it. Absent when NCBI supplies none; it is never defaulted.

edition.description: Edition statement from `Book/Edition`. Rare on Bookshelf titles — absent unless NCBI supplies one.

collectionTitle.description: Series the book belongs to, from `Book/CollectionTitle` (e.g. "ADA Clinical Compendia Series"). Absent for a book outside a series.

isbns.description: Every `Book/Isbn` on the record. A book commonly carries a print and an electronic ISBN, so this is a list. Absent for a Bookshelf title with no ISBN, which is most of them.

items.description: One ISBN, verbatim as NCBI reports it — leading zeros intact

doi.description: The book's own DOI, from `Book/ELocationID` with `EIdType="doi"`. Distinct from the record-level `doi`, which is the chapter's: a chapter does not inherit this one.

editors.description: Editors of the containing book, from `Book/AuthorList` marked `Type="editors"`. Kept out of `authors`, which carries the chapter's own writers. Absent when the book credits no editors.

lastName.description: Editor surname, from the book's `Book/AuthorList Type="editors"` entry. Absent on a group editor, which carries `collectiveName` instead.

firstName.description: Editor given name as NCBI supplies it (`ForeName`, often "Margaret P"). Absent when NCBI carries initials only, or on a group editor.

initials.description: Editor initials with no separators (e.g. "MP"). Absent when NCBI supplies none, or on a group editor.

suffix.description: Editor generational name suffix verbatim from NCBI `Suffix` (e.g. "Jr"). Absent when NCBI supplies none, or on a group editor.

collectiveName.description: Group or committee credited as editor, when the entry names an organization rather than a person. Mutually exclusive with the name-part fields.

items.description: One editor of the containing book. Name parts only — editors are a citation credit, not a contributor record, so no affiliations or ORCID are reported for them.

accession.description: NCBI Bookshelf accession from `ArticleIdList` (`bookaccession`), e.g. "NBK1247". The record is readable at `https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/books/<accession>/`.

book.description: The containing book of a `book-chapter`, or the book itself on a `book` record. Present only on those two record types, and never a stand-in for `journalInfo`.

doi.description: DOI, cased as NCBI reports it (usually the publisher's mixed case). DOIs are case-insensitive by spec and no case normalization is applied here, so the same DOI can arrive in a different case from `pubmed_europepmc_search` and `pubmed_europepmc_fetch` (NCBI `10.1056/NEJMoa2212948`, Europe PMC `10.1056/nejmoa2212948`) — a byte-for-byte comparison across the two reports a false mismatch.

commentsCorrections.description: Records NCBI links to this article — for example retraction notices, errata, expressions of concern, comments, and updates — from `CommentsCorrectionsList`, in NCBI's order and uncapped. `Cites` entries are excluded: they list a bibliography, which `pubmed_find_related` covers with its `references` relationship. Read this alongside `publicationTypes`, not in place of it: that field describes the record itself, and a corrected or questioned article often carries no matching type. Absent when NCBI links nothing other than `Cites` entries, and never set on `book-chapter` or `book` records.

refType.description: Link type, verbatim from NCBI's `RefType` — e.g. "RetractionIn", "RetractionOf", "ErratumIn", "ErratumFor", "ExpressionOfConcernIn", "CommentIn", "CommentOn", "UpdateIn". The set is open: treat an unfamiliar value as opaque.

refSource.description: Citation of the linked record as NCBI writes it (e.g. "Lancet. 2010 Feb 6;375(9713):445. doi: 10.1016/S0140-6736(10)60175-4.").

pmid.description: PMID of the linked record — pass it to `pubmed_fetch_articles` to read that record. Absent when the linked record has no PMID, as with many errata.

note.description: NCBI's note on the link, e.g. what an erratum corrected ("Fuβer, Fabian [corrected to Fußer, Fabian]"). Absent unless NCBI supplies one.

items.description: One record NCBI links to this article and published separately from it — for example a retraction notice, erratum, expression of concern, comment, update, or republication.

isMajorTopic.description: Whether this is a major topic of the article
Whether this qualifier is a major topic

items.description: MeSH qualifier/subheading
MeSH descriptor term

acronym.description: Acronym of the funding institute or agency from `Grant/Acronym` (e.g. "EY" for the National Eye Institute) — it names the funder, never the grant, so it is no substitute for `grantId`.

items.description: Grant record

dataBanks.description: Trial registrations and data deposits the record lists, from NCBI's `DataBankList`, in NCBI's order and uncapped — a ClinicalTrials.gov NCT ID, GenBank and PDB accessions, Dryad and figshare DOIs. To find other PubMed records citing an accession, search `pubmed_search_articles` for `<accession>[si]` (e.g. `NCT03951753[si]`). Counted with the rest of the record under `maxResponseCharacters`. Absent when the record lists none, and never set on `book-chapter` or `book` records.

name.description: Databank or registry name, verbatim from NCBI `DataBankName` (e.g. "ClinicalTrials.gov", "GENBANK", "PDB", "Dryad", "OMIM").

accessionNumbers.description: The record's accessions in this bank, from `AccessionNumberList`, in NCBI's order and uncapped. Absent when NCBI lists the bank without one.

items.description: One accession as NCBI writes it — free text, an all-digit OMIM number or a DOI included (e.g. "NCT03951753", "300460", "10.5061/dryad.8gtht7726")
One databank or registry the record links to, with its accessions there

articleDates.description: Dates of the record itself, each named by `dateType`. On a journal article, PubMed's `ArticleDate` entries (`Electronic` — the electronic publication date). On a Bookshelf record, its own `ContributionDate` (when the chapter was contributed) and `DateRevised` (when it was last updated), distinct from the containing book's dates in `book`; `pubmed_format_citations` cites a chapter by `DateRevised` when present, otherwise `ContributionDate`. Absent when NCBI supplies none.

items.description: Dated article event
Parsed PubMed article

totalReturned.description: Number of articles in this response. Under a `maxResponseCharacters` budget this counts the kept articles only; `deferred.deferredCount` covers the rest.

unavailablePmids.description: PMIDs PubMed returned no record for. That is all this reports: PubMed omits an unknown PMID silently, with no error and no reason, so the absence says nothing about whether the PMID exists. Reported in full regardless of where a `maxResponseCharacters` cutoff lands — these are misses, not deferrals. Use `pubmed_search_articles` to find PMIDs that do resolve.

maxResponseCharacters.description: The `maxResponseCharacters` ceiling this response was budgeted against

returnedCharacters.description: Serialized characters the returned article records account for

deferredCount.description: Articles that resolved but were withheld to stay under the ceiling

ids.description: PMIDs of the deferred articles, in response order. Re-call `pubmed_fetch_articles` with these as `pmids` and the same other inputs to retrieve them. Never contains a PMID from `unavailablePmids`.

nextDeferredCharacters.description: Serialized size of the next deferred article — the first entry in `ids`, where the response stopped — and the continuation ceiling: re-calling with the deferred PMIDs needs `maxResponseCharacters` ≥ this to return anything, and a smaller article further down `ids` cannot be reached until this one fits. Repeating this same call needs `maxResponseCharacters` ≥ `returnedCharacters` + this to return this article as well.

deferred.description: Continuation state for articles the whole-response budget withheld. Present only when `maxResponseCharacters` deferred at least one article.

notice.description: Optional guidance when no articles were returned — points to discovery tools — or when `maxResponseCharacters` deferred articles, naming how to retrieve them. Absent on successful unbudgeted fetches.

truncated.description: True when `maxResponseCharacters` withheld at least one resolved article. Absent when the response carries every article that resolved. The continuation state is in `deferred`.

error.description: Present when the call failed. Absent on success.

code.description: JSON-RPC error code for this failure.

message.description: Human-readable description of what went wrong.

reason.description: Machine-readable failure mode. Declared by this tool: `queue_full`: The local NCBI request queue shed the call — the queue is full, or the call cannot start before its total deadline (for example behind the cooldown that follows an NCBI 429). `ncbi_unreachable`: NCBI E-utilities failed on every attempt the retry budget allowed — retries ran out, or the next backoff would overrun the total deadline. `ncbi_rate_limited`: NCBI answered HTTP 429 (too many requests) and the call stopped on it — retries ran out, the next backoff would overrun the total deadline, or the Retry-After NCBI named outlasts the time left or the 30-second backoff cap. `ncbi_deadline_exceeded`: The total NCBI request deadline expired before NCBI answered successfully — mid-request, while queued, or during a retry backoff. `ncbi_invalid_response`: NCBI returned a body that could not be parsed (invalid XML/JSON). `ncbi_resource_not_found`: NCBI returned a structured "not found" error for the requested ID(s). `invalid_efetch_response`: NCBI EFetch returned a payload missing the PubmedArticleSet wrapper. Other values are possible when a failure originates below the handler.

recovery.description: Actionable next step for the caller.

definition.name: pubmed__pubmed_fetch_fulltext_643cd124
definition.title: Pubmed Fetch Fulltext
definition.description: Fetch full-text articles from PubMed Central as structured sections — the body, then back matter such as acknowledgments, declarations, and appendices — with tables and references. When PMC misses, transparently falls back to Europe PMC `fullTextXML` (structured JATS for its open-access subset, preprints included), then to Unpaywall — publisher-hosted or institutional open-access copies as HTML-as-Markdown or PDF-as-text. Name articles by `pmcids` (PMC IDs directly), `pmids` (PubMed IDs, auto-resolved), `dois` (DOIs, auto-resolved to PMC via the ID Converter; preprints and EPMC-only OA fall through to the Europe PMC and Unpaywall layers), or any mix of the three — up to 50 distinct identifiers; the first 10 are fetched per call, the rest returned in `overLimit`; an article several of them name is fetched and returned once. Two independent character controls: `maxCharacters` caps body text per article, `maxResponseCharacters` caps the whole response and defers articles past the ceiling whole, listing them in `deferred.ids` for a follow-up call.

pmcids.description: PMC IDs to fetch (e.g. ["PMC9575052"]). Combinable with `pmids` and `dois` — up to 50 distinct identifiers across the three; the first 10 are fetched per call, the rest returned in `overLimit`. PMC IDs with no retrievable full text fall through to Europe PMC, then to Unpaywall on the DOI the chain resolves for them.

pmids.description: PubMed IDs. Combinable with `pmcids` and `dois` — up to 50 distinct identifiers across the three; the first 10 are fetched per call, the rest returned in `overLimit`. Articles in PMC are returned as structured JATS; articles not in PMC fall through to Europe PMC (when EPMC has a `fullTextXML`), then to Unpaywall when `UNPAYWALL_EMAIL` is set and a DOI is available.

dois.description: DOIs to resolve (e.g. ["10.21203/rs.3.rs-9010375/v1"]), one per element. Combinable with `pmcids` and `pmids` — up to 50 distinct identifiers across the three; the first 10 are fetched per call, the rest returned in `overLimit`. Resolved to a PMCID via the PMC ID Converter and returned as structured JATS when the article is in PMC; DOIs with no PMC counterpart (preprints, EPMC-only OA) fall through to Europe PMC, then Unpaywall, when those layers are enabled.

includeReferences.description: Include reference list. Applies to `source=pmc` results only.

includeTables.description: Include the article's tables — cells, captions, labels and footnotes. On by default because a dropped table takes its numbers with it. Table-dense articles pay for it: rendered tables typically add 12–17% to an article record and can more than double it. Set false to omit them, or cap the cost with `maxCharacters`, which drops tables it cannot fit whole. Applies to `source=pmc` results only.

includeAssets.description: Include the article's figures and supplementary material — `assets[]`, each with its label, caption, enclosing section and deposit pointer. On by default because it is cheaper than tables: a median asset-bearing article grows about 10%, and the body prose already refers to these by label. Set false to omit them, which also removes the `[Figure: …]` / `[Supplementary: …]` markers from the section text, since without the array they point at nothing. Prose-shaped blocks — lists, definition lists, block quotes, boxed text, preformatted blocks, displayed formulae — are section text rather than assets and this switch never affects them. Applies to `source=pmc` results only.

maxSections.description: Maximum top-level sections, counted after `sections`. Back-matter sections count and follow the body, so a cap drops them first. The sections it drops are named per article in `sectionCap`. Applies to `source=pmc` results only.

sections.description: Filter to specific sections by title (e.g. ["Introduction", "Methods", "Results", "Discussion"]). A term matches a section or subsection title at any nesting depth, case-insensitively, as a substring — "resul" matches "Results". Back-matter sections match the same way: by their own titles, or by their kind when they carry neither a title nor a label — "appendix" matches a section titled "Appendix A", "footnotes" an untitled footnote group. A label is never matched, so an appendix labelled "Appendix A" under a title of its own matches only on that title. A section whose own title matches is returned whole; one kept only because a nested subsection matched keeps its heading as a breadcrumb, with its own text cleared and only the matching branch beneath it. Tables and assets narrow with the filter: one whose section did not survive, or that names no section, is dropped. Empty strings are skipped, so `[""]` applies no filter; an element of only whitespace or invisible characters, such as a zero-width space, is rejected. Applies to `source=pmc` results only.

maxCharacters.description: Per-article budget for body text, in characters. Counts `source=pmc` section and subsection text — which carries the inline blocks the parser renders in place, such as lists, definition lists, block quotes, boxed text, preformatted blocks and displayed formulae — plus table label, caption, cell and footnote text and asset label, caption and `href` text; or the `source=unpaywall` `content` body. Titles, abstracts, identifiers, licenses, and references are never counted or shortened. Shortened text ends at the last word boundary inside its allowance, so it can come back a few characters under it; a section or subsection whose allowance cannot hold its first word returns no text rather than part of that word, so it is dropped in `truncate` mode and heading-only in `outline` mode, while text that is one unbroken token, such as a sequence or URL, is cut at the allowance. The counted unit is that text alone — the Markdown grid `content[]` renders around the cells (pipes, padding, the divider row, headings) is scaffolding this budget does not measure, so a table renders longer than it costs here. Body sections are served first, then tables, then assets, then back-matter sections, each spending what is left, in document order. For tables and assets, admission stops at the first entry that does not fit, and every entry from there on is dropped whole rather than cut mid-row or returned with a shortened caption, counted in `truncation.omittedTables` / `truncation.omittedAssets` and named in `truncation.articles[].omittedTableNames` / `omittedAssetNames`. Back matter takes only what remains and is shortened or dropped as body sections are; `sections` still returns it after the body. Applied after `sections`, `maxSections`, `includeReferences`, `includeTables`, and `includeAssets`, so semantic filtering is unaffected. This knob alone bounds only bodies: the response-wide ceiling it implies is this value times the number of articles returned, plus every uncounted field. Use `maxResponseCharacters` for a true whole-response ceiling. Omit for the full body.

maxCharactersPerSection.description: Budget for a single top-level section, in characters, counting the section text plus its subsections. Combine with `maxCharacters` to cap both one section and the article; the tighter of the two wins. Applies to `source=pmc` results only.

maxResponseCharacters.description: Opt-in ceiling for the whole response, in characters — the true response-wide counterpart to the per-article `maxCharacters`. Each article is measured as the JSON record it is returned as, after every filter and the per-article body budget: title, abstract, sections, references, identifiers, license and source metadata — every field it carries. One ledger covers all tiers, so PMC-, Europe PMC-, and Unpaywall-served articles spend the same budget. Articles are kept in the order `articles` lists them until the next one would cross the ceiling; that article and the rest are deferred whole (never partially populated) and listed in `deferred.ids`. Response envelope fields — counts, `unavailable`, `truncation`, `sectionCap`, `deferred` itself — are not counted. Omit to return every resolved article.

overflowMode.description: How to spend `maxCharacters` across an article that exceeds it. truncate: fill sections in document order, so early sections stay whole, the section the budget runs out in is cut, and every section or subsection past that point is dropped (counted in `truncation.omittedSections`). outline: every section and subsection keeps its heading, and the budget is split evenly at every level — across the top-level sections, then inside each one across its own text and each subsection — with what a short part does not need going to the rest. A part whose share would cut it to under 100 characters (or under `maxCharactersPerSection`, when that is lower) returns heading-only instead, its share going to the others, emptying the last such part first; a part that fits its share keeps all its text however short, and a cut excerpt ends at the last word boundary inside its share, so it can run somewhat under that floor. A heading the budget left empty is marked as such in the rendered text. In both modes the body sections spend the budget first and back-matter sections share what the body, tables, and assets leave. Use it to survey what an article contains before requesting specific `sections`. Ignored when no budget is set, and identical for `source=unpaywall` bodies, which have no headings to preserve.

source.description: Structured JATS — same DTD whether sourced from NCBI PMC or Europe PMC

viaSource.description: Which layer produced the JATS: `pmc` for NCBI PMC EFetch (db=pmc), `europepmc` for Europe PMC `fullTextXML`. Both paths return the same JATS shape; the discriminator records origin for observability and license attribution.

pmcId.description: PMC ID — present for NCBI PMC records and Europe PMC entries that have a PMC counterpart. Absent for EPMC-only records like preprints; use `epmcId` in that case.

pmcUrl.description: PMC URL — derived from `pmcId` when present

doi.description: DOI, cased as the tier that served this record reports it (NCBI PMC, Europe PMC, or Unpaywall). DOIs are case-insensitive by spec and no case normalization is applied here, so casing can differ between tiers and from other tools — compare case-insensitively.

collectiveName.description: Group or consortium name, as the group's own name only: members a deposit nests inside it are not listed here or in `authors`. `pubmed_fetch_articles` with `includeInvestigators` returns a collective author's members from PubMed.

suffix.description: Generational name suffix verbatim from the JATS `<suffix>` (e.g. "Jr", "IV"), never normalized. Absent when the deposit gives none.

items.description: Author entry

elocationId.description: Electronic article locator from JATS `<elocation-id>` — the publisher-assigned article number (e.g. "e20542"). Journals that assign article numbers deposit no `<fpage>`, so this is the only locator on roughly half of PMC records. Never a substitute for `pages`; JATS carries no type attribute, so there is no counterpart to the `elocationIdType` that `pubmed_fetch_articles` reports.

licenses.description: The reuse statements the article's JATS deposits, from NCBI PMC and Europe PMC alike: one entry per `<license>` in its article-meta `<permissions>`, in document order. Figure and table permissions are not included. Relayed as deposited, never interpreted. Absent when the article-meta carries no `<license>`.

text.description: The license's `<license-p>` paragraphs as plain text, a blank line between paragraphs. Absent when the license deposits only a URL.

urls.description: The license's distinct `xlink:href`, then `ali:license_ref` values, as deposited. Absent when the license deposits only text.

items.description: One license statement the article deposits

text.description: Subsection body text. Sections nested deeper than this level are folded in here in document order, each heading rendered on its own line above its text.

items.description: Article subsection
Article section, from the body or from the back matter after it

sections.description: Article sections in source order: the body, then the back matter — acknowledgments, notes and declarations, footnotes, glossary, appendices. A back-matter element with no heading of its own is titled by its kind, such as `Footnotes` or `Appendix`.

tables.description: Every `<table-wrap>` the article carries, in document order — from the body and from `<floats-group>`, `<back>` and appendices alike. Absent when the article deposits none, when `includeTables` is false, or when a `sections` filter left none standing.

label.description: Table label as printed, e.g. `TABLE 1`, less one trailing ` |`, `.` or `:` (`Table 1.` reads `Table 1`)

caption.description: Caption text, with the label excluded

id.description: JATS `id` attribute — the target body-text cross-references point at

sectionTitle.description: Title of the innermost titled section enclosing the table — a body section or a back-matter one such as an appendix — as that section is titled in `sections`, or, for a heading nested deeper than `sections` carries, as its heading line inside the text of the section that contains it. A `sections` filter keeps the table with that section. In back matter the section name is the only positional cue there is. Absent for a table inside no titled section, such as a `<floats-group>` deposit.

headerRowCount.description: How many leading `rows` entries are header rows — a `<thead>` block, or leading rows made entirely of `<th>`. 0 when the table declares none. Several header rows stack: read one column top to bottom for its full header path.

items.description: One row, as cell text by grid column

rows.description: Cell text by row, in document order, one entry per grid column. `colspan` and `rowspan` are expanded, so a cell covering several columns or rows repeats its text across each cell it covers and a well-formed table is rectangular — align on position from the left, and read a repeated value as one spanning cell rather than several measurements. A line break in a cell — a `<break/>`, a paragraph, or a list item in the source — is kept as `\n`, so `1.08\n2.44` is two values; superscripts and other inline markup are never spaced (`0.108a`). Empty when `unextractableReason` is set.

footnotes.description: `<table-wrap-foot>` text, one line per footnote or paragraph, joined by `\n`. A footnote marker deposited as a `<label>` leads its line, followed by a space (`* No patient …`).

unextractableReason.description: Why `rows` is empty — set only then. graphic-only: the table was deposited as an image with no underlying markup. cals-tgroup: the table uses the CALS `<tgroup>` model, which this server does not extract (0 of 283 tables in an open-access survey used it). no-rows: the markup carried no rows. The label and caption are still returned, so a table that could not be read is visible rather than silently missing.

items.description: One table from the article, with its cells, caption, and owning section

assets.description: Every `<fig>` and `<supplementary-material>` the article carries, in document order — from the body and from `<floats-group>`, `<back>` and appendices alike. Each one lifted from a section, body or back matter, leaves a `[Figure: <label>]` or `[Supplementary: <label>]` marker at its position in the section text, so reading order survives the lift. Absent when the article deposits none, when `includeAssets` is false, or when a `sections` filter left none standing.

assetType.description: Which captioned element this came from — `figure` for a `<fig>`, `supplementary-material` for a `<supplementary-material>` deposit

label.description: Display label as printed, e.g. `Fig. 1`, less one trailing ` |`, `.` or `:` (`Figure 1.` reads `Figure 1`). Some supplements carry a bare number (`1`), kept as deposited here

caption.description: Caption text, with the label excluded

id.description: JATS `id` attribute — the target body-text cross-references point at

sectionTitle.description: Title of the innermost titled section enclosing the asset — a body section or a back-matter one such as an appendix — as that section is titled in `sections`, or, for a heading nested deeper than `sections` carries, as its heading line inside the text of the section that contains it. Absent for an asset inside no titled section, such as a `<floats-group>` deposit.

href.description: The `<graphic>`/`<media>` `@xlink:href` exactly as deposited — a pointer into the PMC deposit (`MOL2-20-1253-g001.jpg`), not a fetchable URL. No absolute form of it resolves; read the rendered article at `pmcUrl` instead. Absent when the deposit names no file.

items.description: One figure or supplementary-material item, with its caption, pointer, and section

id.description: Reference ID

items.description: Reference entry

epmcId.description: Europe PMC record id — present when `viaSource` is `europepmc`

epmcSource.description: Europe PMC source code when `viaSource` is `europepmc`. Common values: `MED` (PubMed-derived), `PMC` (PMC counterpart), `PPR` (preprint), `PAT` (patent), `AGR` (Agricola), plus less common codes (`CTX`, `CBA`, `ETH`, `HIR`). Treat as opaque — EPMC may introduce new codes.

oneOf.description: Structured JATS full-text article. `viaSource` records whether the JATS came from NCBI PMC or Europe PMC.

source.description: Content fetched from an open-access copy indexed by Unpaywall. Best-effort — structural fidelity depends on `contentFormat`.

viaSource.description: Layer that produced this article. Constant `unpaywall` for this branch.

contentFormat.description: How `content` was extracted. html-markdown: Defuddle extracted Markdown from an HTML landing page; light section structure may survive but is not guaranteed. pdf-text: unpdf extracted plain text from a PDF; no section, reference, or heading structure.

pmcId.description: PMC ID this article was requested under, in `PMC<digits>` form — present when a `pmcids` entry named it, absent when it was requested under a PMID or DOI. When several identifiers name one article, it is requested under the first to reach it: `pmcids`, then `pmids`, then `dois`. Ties the article back to the requested identifier, which `unavailable[]` keys on for the ids that found nothing.

pmid.description: PubMed ID this article was requested under — present when it was requested under a `pmids` entry, absent when under a PMC ID or DOI (see `pmcId` for which identifier an article several of them name is requested under)

pubmedUrl.description: PubMed URL — present when `pmid` is set

doi.description: DOI used to locate the open-access copy

sourceUrl.description: URL the content was fetched from

title.description: Article title, from the first source that carries one: Unpaywall's record for the DOI, then the Europe PMC record when the chain searched Europe PMC for this id, then — for `html-markdown` content only — the title detected on the page. Absent when none of them has a title.

journalName.description: Journal or repository name from Unpaywall's record for the DOI (e.g. `medRxiv` for a medRxiv preprint). Absent when Unpaywall has none.

year.description: Publication year from Unpaywall's record for the DOI. Absent when Unpaywall has none.

content.description: Full article text — Markdown or plain text per `contentFormat`

wordCount.description: Approximate word count reported by the HTML extractor; absent for PDFs

totalPages.description: Page count reported by the PDF extractor; absent for HTML

license.description: License identifier from Unpaywall (e.g. cc-by, cc0)

hostType.description: `publisher` or `repository` — where the OA copy is hosted

oneOf.description: Best-effort full text from an open-access copy

items.description: Full-text article; shape depends on `source` (pmc = structured JATS, unpaywall = best-effort)

articles.description: Full-text articles in routing order — `pmcids`, then `pmids`, then `dois`, request order within each — each at the position of the id it would be deferred under, whichever tier served it. An article several ids name appears once.

totalReturned.description: Number of articles in this response. Under a `maxResponseCharacters` budget this counts the kept articles only; `deferred.deferredCount` covers the rest.

unavailable.description: Per-identifier explanations for any requested PMIDs, PMCIDs, or DOIs with no returnable full text. `idType` names the field each id was sent in. Distinct from `deferred`: nothing here is retrievable by re-calling, and an id never appears in both. Ids past the per-call limit are listed in `overLimit`, never here.

id.description: Identifier the chain could not resolve — PMID, PMCID, or DOI per `idType`

idType.description: Which input field the id was sent in — `pmids`, `pmcids`, or `dois` respectively

reason.description: Why no full text was returned — the most specific signal any tier that answered reported. not-found: upstream returned no record for this ID. no-pmc-fallback-disabled: every tier was skipped (`triedTiers` is all `not-attempted`) — typically because EPMC (`EUROPEPMC_ENABLED`) and Unpaywall (`UNPAYWALL_EMAIL`) are not configured. no-epmc-fulltext: EPMC indexed the record but publishes no fullTextXML. no-body: the record was retrieved but carries front matter and abstract only, with no body sections — use `pubmed_fetch_articles` for the metadata. no-doi: the DOI lookup ran and this record has none, so Unpaywall could not be queried. doi-lookup-failed: the DOI lookup itself errored, so whether a DOI exists is unknown and Unpaywall was never reached — retry the request; unlike no-doi this is a transient failure, not a settled answer. no-oa: Unpaywall has no OA copy. fetch-failed: download failed. parse-failed: extraction empty. service-error: upstream server failure (threw, timed out, or returned malformed data). A reason never means the chain ran to completion — read `unqueriedTiers` for that.

tier.description: Which tier in the resolution chain

outcome.description: Per-tier outcome. not-attempted: tier was skipped. miss: tier returned no record. no-fulltext: EPMC indexed the record but publishes no fullTextXML. no-body: the tier returned a record with front matter and abstract but no body sections, so the chain continued. no-doi: the DOI lookup ran and this record has none, so Unpaywall could not be queried. doi-lookup-failed: the DOI lookup itself errored, so whether a DOI exists is unknown and Unpaywall was never reached — retry the request. no-oa: Unpaywall reports no open-access copy. fetch-failed: OA copy download failed. parse-failed: extraction produced empty content. service-error: tier service threw.

items.description: One tier the resolution chain attempted, with its outcome

triedTiers.description: Per-tier outcomes the chain produced for this id, in execution order. Covers `pmc`, `europepmc`, and `unpaywall` — the same tiers the tool description references. Tiers that the chain skipped appear as `outcome: not-attempted` with a `detail` explaining why.

unqueriedTiers.description: Tiers the chain skipped because this deployment has not configured them, and that could have served this id — the search was incomplete, and a deployment with these tiers configured may still resolve the id. `triedTiers` carries which environment variable each one is waiting on. Absent when every tier that could have served the id was actually queried; a tier skipped because it was inapplicable to this id (no DOI for Unpaywall) is never listed.

items.description: A fallback tier this deployment has not configured
One identifier that could not be returned, with the full chain it traversed

originalCharacters.description: Body characters the shortened articles carried before the budget pass

returnedCharacters.description: Body characters the shortened articles carry in this response

omittedSections.description: Sections and subsections, back matter included, dropped entirely because an article budget was exhausted before reaching them. Back matter is reached last, after tables and assets. A dropped section counts once, together with its subsections. Always 0 in `outline` mode, which keeps every heading.

omittedTables.description: Tables dropped whole across every budgeted article, because the budget left no room once body sections were served. Absent when none were dropped. Re-request the affected articles with a higher `maxCharacters`, or with `sections` narrowed, to receive them.

omittedAssets.description: Figures and supplementary items dropped whole across every budgeted article, because the budget left no room once body sections and tables were served. Absent when none were dropped. Re-request the affected articles with a higher `maxCharacters`, or with `sections` narrowed, to receive them.

id.description: Identifier for the article — PMCID, PMID, DOI, or Europe PMC id, whichever the article carries first

source.description: Which output shape was budgeted: `pmc` budgets sections and subsections, `unpaywall` budgets the single `content` body

originalCharacters.description: Body characters this article carried before the budget pass

returnedCharacters.description: Body characters this article carries in the response

sections.description: Per-section accounting for `source: pmc` articles, in document order, including sections dropped for budget; a shortened section lists its subsections. Absent for `source: unpaywall`, whose body has no section structure.

title.description: Section heading, when the section carries one

label.description: Section label as printed (e.g. `2`), when the section carries one

originalCharacters.description: Body characters this section carried before the budget pass

returnedCharacters.description: Body characters this section carries in the response. Zero means the section was dropped in `truncate` mode, or kept as a heading-only entry in `outline` mode, marked as such in the rendered text.

truncated.description: True when the section returned fewer characters than it originally carried

subsections.description: Per-subsection accounting for a shortened section, in document order, including subsections dropped for budget — where inside the section the cut landed. Absent when the section was returned whole or carries no subsections.

title.description: Subsection heading, when the subsection carries one

label.description: Subsection label as printed (e.g. `2.1`), when the subsection carries one

originalCharacters.description: Body characters this subsection carried before the budget pass

returnedCharacters.description: Body characters this subsection carries in the response. Zero means it was dropped in `truncate` mode and counted in `omittedSections`, or kept as a heading-only entry in `outline` mode, marked as such in the rendered text.

truncated.description: True when the subsection returned fewer characters than it originally carried

items.description: Character accounting for one subsection of a shortened section
Character accounting for one section of a budgeted article

omittedTables.description: Tables this article dropped whole because the budget left no room for them. A table is never cut mid-row, so it is either returned complete or counted here. Absent when none were dropped.

omittedTableNames.description: The dropped tables by name, in document order — each table's label, else its `id`, else `table <n>` for its position in the article. Names the tables a bare count only hints at, the way `deferred.ids` names deferred articles. Every table from the first that did not fit onward is here: admission stops at that table rather than skipping ahead to a smaller one, so these are contiguous. Absent when none were dropped.

omittedAssets.description: Figures and supplementary items this article dropped whole because the budget left no room once body sections and tables were served. An asset is never returned with a truncated caption, so it is either returned complete or counted here. Absent when none were dropped.

omittedAssetNames.description: The dropped assets by name, in document order — each asset's label (a bare-number label led by its type, `Supplementary material 1`), else its `id`, else `asset <n>` for its position in the article. Contiguous for the same reason `omittedTableNames` is: admission stops at the first asset that did not fit rather than skipping ahead to a smaller one. Absent when none were dropped.

items.description: Character accounting for one article the budget shortened

articles.description: Per-article accounting, covering only the articles the budget shortened

truncation.description: Character accounting for full text the budget shortened. Present only when a budget actually removed characters — its absence means every returned article carries its full post-filter body.

id.description: Identifier for the article — PMCID, PMID, DOI, or Europe PMC id, whichever the article carries first; the id `truncation.articles[].id` uses

title.description: Section heading, when the section carries one

label.description: Section label as printed (e.g. `2`), when the section carries one

items.description: One top-level section the cap left out

omittedSections.description: The top-level sections past the cap, in document order, back matter included — counted after the `sections` filter, so a section the filter excluded is not here. The article returned the first `maxSections` top-level sections and had `maxSections` plus this many.

items.description: The top-level sections one article lost to `maxSections`

articles.description: Per-article lists, in the order `articles` lists the articles, covering only the returned articles the cap cut

sectionCap.description: The top-level sections `maxSections` left out of `source: pmc` articles, PMC- and Europe PMC-served alike. Present only when the cap dropped at least one section from a returned article. Separate from `truncation`, which accounts for characters a budget removed from the sections the cap kept: no section appears in both. Re-call with `sections` set to the titles you need, or with a larger `maxSections`, to receive them.

maxResponseCharacters.description: The `maxResponseCharacters` ceiling this response was budgeted against

returnedCharacters.description: Serialized characters the returned article records account for

deferredCount.description: Articles the chain resolved but withheld to stay under the ceiling

definition.name: pubmed__pubmed_spell_check_11d9b003
definition.title: Pubmed Spell Check
definition.description: Spell-check a PubMed search query against NCBI ESpell and get the corrected query back. Use after a zero-hit or thin `pubmed_search_articles` result, or when a drug, gene, disease, or author name may be misspelled. Corrections are applied in place, so field tags, operators, spacing, and gene symbols stay as written (`alzhiemer diseese treatmnt outcomse` → `alzheimer disease treatment outcomes`). The value of an indexed field — MeSH, publication type, journal, author, language, subset, and the like (`aged[mh]`, `free full text[sb]`, `zhang y[au]`) — is kept as written, misspelled or not, since the ESpell dictionary is not the index that field searches; free-text fields such as `[tiab]`, `[ti]`, and `[tw]` are corrected. Re-run the search with `corrected`.

definition.name: pubmed__pubmed_fetch_citation_metrics_413f9b41
definition.title: Pubmed Fetch Citation Metrics
definition.description: Fetch NIH iCite citation metrics for PubMed articles: the Relative Citation Ratio (RCR), NIH percentile, citation count, citations per year, expected and field citation rates, the Approximate Potential to Translate (APT), the human, animal, and molecular/cellular shares of each article's MeSH terms, and how many clinical articles cite it. RCR is a field- and year-normalized citation rate benchmarked to NIH-funded papers, whose median RCR is 1.0; iCite computes none for the most recent papers and marks recent ones provisional. iCite does not flag retractions — a retracted article keeps its metrics — so check pubmed_fetch_articles for retraction notices before relying on a record. Up to 1000 PMIDs per call; the first 200 distinct PMIDs are fetched and the rest returned in `overLimit`. PMIDs iCite has no record for are listed in `unavailablePmids`.

pmids.description: PubMed IDs to look up (e.g. ["23456789"]). The first 200 distinct PMIDs are fetched; the rest are returned in `overLimit`. Leading zeros are ignored, so "00023456789" and "23456789" name one article.

title.description: Article title as display-ready plain text — markup stripped and HTML entities decoded. Absent when iCite carries none.

year.description: iCite's publication year: the year of the published version, which can differ from PubMed's publication date.

journal.description: Journal abbreviation as iCite reports it.

doi.description: DOI when iCite carries one.

isResearchArticle.description: Whether iCite classes the record as a primary research article; reviews, editorials, letters, and errata are not.

isClinical.description: Whether iCite classes the article as clinical research.

relativeCitationRatio.description: Relative Citation Ratio (RCR): the article's citations per year divided by the citations per year expected for its field, benchmarked so the median NIH-funded paper of the same year scores 1.0. Absent when iCite computes none — papers too recent to benchmark, and some older records.

rcrProvisional.description: True when iCite marks the RCR provisional: a recent paper whose RCR can change as citations accrue. Present only beside `relativeCitationRatio`.

nihPercentile.description: Percentile (0–100) of the article's RCR among NIH-funded papers. Absent when iCite reports none, as for papers before 1980 and for most-recent-year provisional RCRs.

citationCount.description: Citations iCite counts for the article. Absent when the record is not yet scored.

citationsPerYear.description: Citations per year since publication, the numerator of the RCR.

expectedCitationsPerYear.description: Citations per year expected for an article in this one's field and year, the denominator of the RCR.

fieldCitationRate.description: Citation rate of the article's co-citation network — the field benchmark the expected rate is derived from.

apt.description: Approximate Potential to Translate: iCite's estimate of the likelihood that a clinical article will cite this one, reported as 0.05, 0.25, 0.75, or 0.95.

human.description: Share (0–1) of the article's MeSH terms in the Human category.

animal.description: Share (0–1) of the article's MeSH terms in the Animal category.

molecularCellular.description: Share (0–1) of the article's MeSH terms in the Molecular/Cellular category.

citedByClinicalArticle.description: Whether at least one clinical article cites this one.

clinicalCitationCount.description: Clinical articles citing this one: 0 when `citedByClinicalArticle` is false, absent when that flag is.

items.description: NIH iCite citation metrics for one PubMed article

records.description: One record per fetched PMID iCite knows, in request order.

unavailablePmids.description: Requested PMIDs within the per-call limit that NIH iCite has no record for, in request order, under the spelling sent. iCite omits a PMID it has no record for without an error, so the absence says nothing about whether PubMed has the article; pubmed_fetch_articles confirms that.

limit.description: Distinct PMIDs one call fetches. The first this many, in request order, were fetched; the PMIDs below were not.

pmids.description: PMIDs past the per-call limit, none of them fetched, in request order — each listed once, under the first spelling sent. Re-call `pubmed_fetch_citation_metrics` with these as `pmids`, at most `limit` per call.

overLimit.description: PMIDs the call named past the per-call fetch limit. Present only when the call named more distinct PMIDs than one call fetches.

notice.description: Names the PMIDs iCite had no record for, records not yet scored, records with no RCR or a provisional one, and PMIDs past the per-call limit with how to fetch them. Absent when every record came back final and complete.

error.description: Present when the call failed. Absent on success.

code.description: JSON-RPC error code for this failure.
