definition.name: pubchem__pubchem_get_compound_interactions_b1275861
definition.title: Get Compound Interactions
definition.description: Get a compound's interaction data: drug-food interactions, and the molecular targets its bioassays name — one entry per target as kinds defines it, with its assay counts by outcome and most potent active value, Active targets first, most potent first. Each entry carries its originating source. Results are paged per kind, with the record total and the next offset reported for each. Drug-food coverage is richest for approved drugs; target covers any compound PubChem has assay data for, and pubchem_get_bioactivity lists one target's assays when given the entry's GeneID or accession. Drug-drug interactions (DrugBank) are unavailable while PubChem's SDQ service refuses automated requests: an explicit drug-drug request is reported in failedKinds while the other kinds still return.

cid.description: PubChem Compound ID. Resolve from name/SMILES with pubchem_search_compounds.

kinds.description: Interaction kinds to fetch. "drug-food" (dietary interactions, from PUG View), "target" (molecular targets from the compound's assay summary: one entry per Gene ID with the accessions the table pairs with it, and one per identifier it never pairs, so a Gene ID and an accession that no row pairs are separate entries even when they name the same protein), "drug-drug" (interactions with other drugs, from PubChem's SDQ service, which refuses automated requests, so it is reported in failedKinds). Default: ["drug-food"].

offset.description: Zero-based start position within each requested kind, counted in records (molecular targets, for target) rather than returned entries. The same offset applies to every kind in the call, and the kinds advance at different rates — when paging past the first page, request one kind per call and pass that kind's nextOffset. Default: 0.

maxEntries.description: Max entries per kind per page. The per-call cap is 50: a larger value (up to 1000) reads a page of 50 per kind and is reported in cappedInputs. Well-studied drugs have a long tail of interactions; use offset to reach the ones past this page. Default: 10.

kind.description: Interaction category.

partner.description: Interacting compound as the source reports it. For a target: its gene or protein name and organism, then the identifier pubchem_get_bioactivity filters on (GeneID:N → targetGeneId, accession:X → targetAccession); the identifier alone when no name resolves. A target whose identifiers join several Gene IDs is named by the accession they share and says "group of N Gene IDs".

source.description: Originating source (e.g. "DrugBank", "PubChem BioAssay").

text.description: The interaction statement. For a target: the assays naming it by outcome and its most potent Active value with that AID, in µM.

items.description: A single interaction entry.

entries.description: Interaction entries across the requested kinds.

kind.description: Interaction category this page covers.

returnedCount.description: Interaction entries returned for this kind.

totalRecords.description: Records available for this kind, across all pages: interaction records for drug-drug and drug-food, molecular targets for target. Entries are derived from these records and can be fewer: a drug-drug record carrying no statement yields nothing. Pages divide the records, not the entries.

nextOffset.description: Offset to pass on the next call to continue this kind past the current page. Omitted when no records remain.

truncated.description: True when source records remain for this kind past the current page.

items.description: Page position for one interaction kind.

paging.description: Per-kind page position, one entry per requested kind that was retrieved. A kind listed in failedKinds is absent — its position is unknown, not exhausted.

returnedCount.description: Total interaction entries returned across all kinds.

truncated.description: True when at least one requested kind has source records remaining past this page. Which kinds, and how many records each holds, is in paging[].truncated / paging[].totalRecords.

offset.description: Zero-based start position read within each requested kind.

nextOffset.description: Offset to pass on the next call, reported when exactly one requested kind has records remaining. Omitted when none do, and when several do — those advance to different positions, so read paging[].nextOffset instead.

failedKinds.description: Interaction kinds that could not be retrieved (comma-separated). The returned entries cover the kinds that succeeded. The notice says, per failed kind, whether a retry can help: a timeout, rate limit, network error, unreadable response, or upstream 5xx other than 501 can clear, while an HTTP 400, 403, or 501, a response in a shape the server does not expect, or a refusal from PubChem's SDQ service (drug-drug) does not.

notice.description: Guidance when a kind failed, when no interaction data was found, when the offset runs past every requested kind, when target names could not be retrieved, or when further pages remain. Absent when this page is complete and every kind resolved.

cappedInputs.description: Inputs that asked for more than their per-call cap, with the value requested and the value served. An ID batch lists the IDs past the cap in unprocessed. Omitted when every input was within its cap.

requested.description: Value requested: the page size, or the number of IDs in the batch.

unprocessed.description: ID batches only: IDs past the cap, listed in unprocessed in input order.

items.description: One input served at its per-call cap.

error.description: Present when the call failed. Absent on success.

code.description: JSON-RPC error code for this failure.

message.description: Human-readable description of what went wrong.

reason.description: Machine-readable failure mode.

recovery.description: Actionable next step for the caller.

definition.name: pubchem__pubchem_search_assays_8429d2ac
definition.title: Search Assays
definition.description: Find PubChem bioassays associated with a biological target. Search by gene symbol (e.g. "EGFR"), protein name, NCBI Gene ID, or UniProt accession. Returns a page of assay IDs (AIDs) — page past maxResults with offset — which can be explored further with pubchem_get_summary.

targetType.description: Target identifier type. "genesymbol" and "proteinname" accept text names; a genesymbol matches the symbol case-insensitively across species, so a human symbol also returns assays on other species' orthologs. "geneid" accepts NCBI Gene IDs. "proteinaccession" accepts UniProt accessions. "geneid" and "proteinaccession" each pin one protein, but return overlapping, different assay sets for it, since PubChem records some assays under only one of the two identifiers; for a complete list for one protein, union both.

targetQuery.description: Target identifier. Examples: "EGFR" (genesymbol), "Epidermal growth factor receptor" (proteinname), "1956" (geneid), "P00533" (proteinaccession; uppercased before lookup, except a PDB chain ID such as the "A" in "1ZHH_A", which is kept as given).

offset.description: Zero-based index of the first AID to return. Pass the nextOffset from a previous call to read the following page. Default: 0.

maxResults.description: Max AIDs to return per page. The per-call cap is 200: a larger value (up to 1000) returns a page of 200 and is reported in cappedInputs. Popular targets may have thousands of assays; use offset to reach the ones past this page. Default: 50.

targetType.description: Target identifier type used: genesymbol, proteinname, geneid, or proteinaccession.

totalFound.description: Total AIDs found for this target, across all pages.

offset.description: Zero-based index of the first AID returned.

nextOffset.description: Offset to pass on the next call to continue past this page. Omitted when no further AIDs match.

truncated.description: True when matching AIDs remain past this page.

cap.description: The page size applied: maxResults, or the per-call cap when maxResults exceeds it.

cappedInputs.description: Inputs that asked for more than their per-call cap, with the value requested and the value served. An ID batch lists the IDs past the cap in unprocessed. Omitted when every input was within its cap.

requested.description: Value requested: the page size, or the number of IDs in the batch.

unprocessed.description: ID batches only: IDs past the cap, listed in unprocessed in input order.

items.description: One input served at its per-call cap.

notice.description: Recovery guidance when no assays matched, when the offset runs past the result set, or when further pages remain. Absent when this page is complete and non-empty.

error.description: Present when the call failed. Absent on success.

code.description: JSON-RPC error code for this failure.

message.description: Human-readable description of what went wrong.

reason.description: Machine-readable failure mode. Declared by this tool: `blank_target_query`: targetQuery is empty or whitespace-only. `invalid_geneid_query`: targetType is "geneid" but targetQuery contains characters other than digits. `target_query_rejected`: PubChem refused the target lookup with HTTP 400 — its answer for a targetQuery carrying a line break, another C0 control character other than tab and NUL, or DEL. Other values are possible when a failure originates below the handler.

recovery.description: Actionable next step for the caller.

definition.name: pubchem__pubchem_get_summary_12ee3fb7
definition.title: Get Entity Summary
definition.description: Get descriptive summaries for PubChem entities by ID. Supports assays (AID), genes (Gene ID), proteins (UniProt accession), and taxonomy (Tax ID). Up to 10 per call; identifiers past that are returned in unprocessed for a follow-up call.

entityType.description: Entity type. Determines ID format and returned fields.

items.description: Entity identifier, or several joined with commas.

identifiers.description:
Entity identifiers. A comma-joined string is split into one identifier per piece, with whitespace trimmed. The per-call cap is 10 pieces: the first 10 are looked up, and any past that are returned in unprocessed, in input order, and reported in cappedInputs. More than 1000 pieces in all fails the call. ID form depends on entityType:
- assay: AID, a positive integer, e.g. ["1000"]
- gene: NCBI Gene ID, a positive integer, e.g. ["1956"]
- protein: UniProt accession, e.g. ["P00533"]
- taxonomy: NCBI Taxonomy ID, a positive integer, e.g. ["9606"]
For assay, gene, and taxonomy, a piece that is not a positive integer up to 2147483647 written in digits is marked invalid and not looked up.

anyOf.description: Numeric identifier (e.g. AID, Gene ID, Tax ID).

identifier.description: Queried identifier: a number for assay, gene, and taxonomy; the accession for protein; the piece as sent when invalid.

invalid.description: True when the identifier is not in the form entityType expects; it was not looked up. Omitted otherwise.

data.description: Entity summary data. Populated fields depend on entityType.

aid.description: Assay ID — present on assay summaries.

method.description: Assay method as PubChem labels it (assay summaries): "confirmatory" (dose-response), "screening" (primary screen), "summary", or "other". Omitted when PubChem records none.

targets.description: Assay targets, the first 25 PubChem lists (assay summaries); targetCount gives the full number.

items.description: Assay target.

targetCount.description: Number of targets PubChem lists for the assay (assay summaries).

numCompounds.description: Compounds (CIDs) tested (assay summaries). List them with pubchem_search_compounds searchType "assay" and activeOnly: false — its default lists only the actives.

numActiveCompounds.description: Compounds (CIDs) the assay marked active (assay summaries).

lastDataChange.description: Date the assay's data last changed, YYYY-MM-DD (assay summaries).

lineage.description: Taxonomic lineage ordered from the most inclusive rank to the most specific, e.g. ["Eukaryota", "Metazoa", "Chordata"] (taxonomy summaries). Ranks that do not apply to the entity are omitted.

items.description: Per-identifier summary result.

summaries.description: Summary results, one per identifier piece looked up, in input order.

unprocessed.description: Identifier pieces past the per-call cap of 10, in input order, not looked up. Pass them in a follow-up call. Omitted when every piece was served.

requestedCount.description: Identifier pieces requested, counted after comma splitting.

notice.description: Recovery guidance when identifiers were invalid or not found.

cappedInputs.description: Inputs that asked for more than their per-call cap, with the value requested and the value served. An ID batch lists the IDs past the cap in unprocessed. Omitted when every input was within its cap.

requested.description: Value requested: the page size, or the number of IDs in the batch.

unprocessed.description: ID batches only: IDs past the cap, listed in unprocessed in input order.

items.description: One input served at its per-call cap.

error.description: Present when the call failed. Absent on success.

code.description: JSON-RPC error code for this failure.

message.description: Human-readable description of what went wrong.

reason.description: Machine-readable failure mode. Declared by this tool: `too_many_identifiers`: Comma splitting yields more than 1000 identifier pieces. `invalid_identifier`: No identifier piece is usable: every piece is blank, or, for assay, gene, or taxonomy, not a positive integer up to 2147483647. Other values are possible when a failure originates below the handler.

recovery.description: Actionable next step for the caller.

definition.name: openalex__openalex_resolve_name_db574658
definition.title: Openalex Resolve Name
definition.description: Resolve a name or an identifier to an OpenAlex ID. ALWAYS use this before filtering by entity — names are ambiguous, IDs are not. A name returns up to 10 autocomplete matches with disambiguation hints. An identifier — OpenAlex ID, DOI, ORCID, ROR, PMID, or ISSN, bare or in URL form — resolves directly to the record it addresses instead of running a name search. Short names share the bare OpenAlex ID shape (keyword p53 reads as publisher ID P53), so a bare OpenAlex ID that resolves nothing is searched as a name next. Two identifiers can address more than one entity type: a ROR names an organization's institution, funder, and publisher records alike, so it returns each one that exists (institution first) unless entity_type picks one of those three; and a Crossref Funder Registry DOI (10.13039/…) resolves to the funder unless entity_type is works. A PMCID is recognized as well, bare or as a PubMed Central URL, but OpenAlex indexes no PMCIDs, so it resolves nothing — pass the work's PMID or DOI instead. An award ID (G…, bare or as an OpenAlex URL) is not looked up, since OpenAlex has no award autocomplete: it returns no matches and a notice naming the openalex_search_entities call that opens the award. Under entity_type, a bare G… is searched as a name of that type instead.

entity_type.description: Entity type to search. Awards are not among them: OpenAlex has no award autocomplete, so search awards with openalex_search_entities. Omit for cross-entity search (useful when entity type is unknown). With an identifier `query` it narrows only an identifier that can address more than one type: a ROR to institutions, funders, or publishers (omit it to get every one of the three that exists), and a Funder Registry DOI (10.13039/…) to works instead of the funder. Every other identifier resolves as the type it belongs to, whatever this names — except under keywords, where a bare OpenAlex ID shape ("P53") is searched as a keyword name, since keyword IDs are slugs.

query.description: Name or partial name to resolve. Also accepts an identifier, bare or in URL form — OpenAlex ID ("W2741809807", "F4320332161", or an OpenAlex record-page or API URL such as "https://openalex.org/works/W2741809807"), DOI ("10.1038/nature12373", or a funder's Funder Registry DOI such as "10.13039/100000001"), ORCID ("0000-0002-1825-0097"), ROR ("https://ror.org/00hx57361"), PMID ("12345678" or "https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/12345678"), ISSN ("1234-5678") — which resolves straight to the record it addresses, or for a ROR up to three (see entity_type), instead of running a name search. A bare OpenAlex ID that resolves nothing is then searched as a name — under entity_type when given, and not at all when filters come without entity_type — since short names share its shape ("P53" is a keyword); under entity_type keywords it is searched as a name from the start. A keyword URL ("https://openalex.org/keywords/groundwater") resolves the same way; a bare keyword slug reads as a name and runs a name search, which finds it too. A PMCID ("PMC1234567" or a PubMed Central URL) is recognized but OpenAlex indexes no PMCIDs, so it resolves nothing — pass the work's PMID or DOI instead. An award ID ("G417894356", or "https://openalex.org/awards/G417894356") sends no request and names the openalex_search_entities call for it; with entity_type, a bare one is searched as a name of that type.

filters.description: Narrow autocomplete results with a filter record object, using the openalex_search_entities value syntax; native string input is unavailable here. Example: restrict to a specific country or publication year range. Country fields take ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 codes ({"country_code": "DE"} on institutions) and `language` takes ISO 639-1 codes ("en"); alpha-3, numeric, ISO 639-2, and English-name forms are converted — a multi-word name is one value, so "South Korea|Japan" ORs two countries — and a value that cannot be a country code is rejected. A multi-word value on a field matched as whole text (display_name, geo.city, geo.region, awards.funder_display_name) matches as one phrase ({"geo.city": "New York"} on institutions; a comma, as in "University of California, Berkeley", is part of it, and it cannot contain a double quote of its own), "!" and "|" included, but cannot be ANDed with "+" in the same field. A value sent unquoted must have paired double quotes; balanced search phrases remain valid. A value mixing "|" with an AND operator — a "+", or a space on a field where words mean AND — is rejected, since OpenAlex drops every "|" alternative that ANDs more than one value; put the AND in a second key instead. Requires entity_type — filter fields belong to one entity type, so a name search across every type takes none, and a name query passing filters without entity_type is rejected. Applies to name queries only — an identifier lookup returns the records it addresses regardless.

id.description: OpenAlex ID.

external_id.description: Canonical external ID (DOI, ORCID, ROR, ISSN).

display_name.description: Human-readable name as plain text, with HTML entities decoded and markup removed. null only for an identifier lookup that landed on a record OpenAlex holds no title for (paratext works and other untitled entries) — use `id` to identify it.

entity_type.description: Entity type — one of: work, author, source, institution, topic, keyword, publisher, funder.

cited_by_count.description: Citation count (direct for works, aggregate for others).

works_count.description: Associated works. null for works themselves.

hint.description: Disambiguation context as plain text — last institution (authors), host organization (sources), place or country (institutions); author names (works) from a name search, publication year from an identifier lookup. null when the record carries none.

items.description: A single autocomplete match with its ID, name, entity type, activity stats, and a disambiguation hint.

results.description: Matches: up to 10 autocomplete matches for a name; for an identifier, the record it addresses — for a ROR, up to three, institution then funder then publisher — or none.

notice.description: Guidance notice. Set when nothing matched (echoes the query, and the filters when a name search applied them, and suggests corrections), when a bare OpenAlex ID resolved nothing and the query was searched as a name instead (names both outcomes, or why the name search did not run or finish), when an identifier query was passed name-search parameters that do not apply to it, when one of the lookups for a ROR failed upstream (names the entity type whose record may be missing), or when the query is an award ID (names the openalex_search_entities call that opens it). Caller text in it is JSON-encoded and Markdown-escaped, the same string on both surfaces. Absent otherwise.

budget.description: What this call cost against the OpenAlex daily budget and what is left of it. Read `remainingUsd` here to size the search or traversal this resolution feeds. Absent when OpenAlex omitted the accounting headers.

costUsd.description: USD this call spent. Autocomplete is priced at the floor — resolving a name before filtering costs far less than the failed searches an ambiguous name causes.

remainingUsd.description: USD left in today's OpenAlex budget after this call.

resetsInSeconds.description: Seconds until the daily budget refills (midnight UTC).

prepaidRemainingUsd.description: USD left in the prepaid balance — a separate pool OpenAlex draws on only after the daily allowance runs out, and which the daily reset does not refill. Add it to `remainingUsd` for the full spendable amount. Absent when the account holds no prepaid balance.

error.description: Present when the call failed. Absent on success.

code.description: JSON-RPC error code for this failure.

message.description: Human-readable description of what went wrong.

reason.description: Machine-readable failure mode. Declared by this tool: `unmatched_quote_in_filter_value`: A filter value sent unquoted has an unmatched double quote. `filters_without_entity_type`: A name `query` passed `filters` without `entity_type`. Filter fields belong to one entity type, and a name search across every type takes no filters. `rate_limited`: OpenAlex throttled the autocomplete request for exceeding its per-second ceiling (HTTP 429). `upstream_budget_exhausted`: The OpenAlex daily usage budget is spent (HTTP 429). `upstream_plan_required`: A filter is one OpenAlex serves only on a paid plan — created_date, updated_date, or a from_/to_ form of either (HTTP 429 "Plan upgrade required"). `upstream_timeout`: OpenAlex did not respond within the request deadline. `upstream_unavailable`: OpenAlex was unreachable or unusable — HTTP 503, a connection failure, or a body that was empty, HTML, or unparseable JSON. `upstream_unauthorized`: OpenAlex rejected the API key (HTTP 401). `upstream_forbidden`: OpenAlex denied access to autocomplete (HTTP 403). `id_dot_segment`: An identifier `query` holds a `.` or `..` path segment, written plainly or percent-encoded. `comma_in_filter_value`: A `filters` value contains a comma, which collides with the OpenAlex filter separator, on a field that takes no phrase. Free-text search filters (any `.search` key, such as display_name.search) and fields matched as whole text (display_name, awards.funder_display_name, awards.funder_award_id, geo.city, geo.region, raw_affiliation_strings, block_key, parsed_longest_name, biblio fields) are exempt: a comma there is sent quoted, as part of the phrase. `invalid_country_code`: A country filter (a key ending in country_code, country_codes, or countries) holds a segment that cannot be a country code, such as a misspelled name, an unassigned number, "unknown", or two codes joined by a space ("DE US"). `mixed_and_or_in_filter_value`: A `filters` value puts "|" (OR) beside an AND operator — a "+", or a space on a field where words mean AND (on a country field a space is always part of a country name, and inside a language name it is part of the name). OpenAlex splits the value on "|" first and drops every alternative that ANDs more than one value, so no single value can carry both. `quote_in_filter_value`: A `filters` value sent to OpenAlex double-quoted holds a double quote inside its outer pair — a value the server quotes (a multi-word value on a field matched as whole text, or a value holding a comma on such a field or on a free-text search filter), or one the caller wrapped in double quotes on any filter but a free-text search. `upstream_invalid_params`: OpenAlex rejected an invalid filter field name on the autocomplete query (HTTP 400). `upstream_invalid_id_value`: A `filters` entry expecting an entity ID received a value that is not an OpenAlex ID — usually a name (HTTP 400). `query_too_long`: OpenAlex autocomplete failed (HTTP 500) on a `query` longer than the 1,000 characters it accepts when entity_type is set. `upstream_invalid_params_other`: OpenAlex rejected the autocomplete request (HTTP 400) for a reason other than an invalid field name. `upstream_validation_failed`: OpenAlex rejected the autocomplete request as semantically invalid (HTTP 422). Other values are possible when a failure originates below the handler.

recovery.description: Actionable next step for the caller.

definition.name: openalex__openalex_search_entities_687af289
definition.title: Openalex Search Entities
definition.description: Search, filter, sort, or retrieve by ID. Covers all OpenAlex entity types (works, authors, sources, institutions, topics, keywords, publishers, funders, awards). Pass `id` to retrieve a single entity. Otherwise, use `query` and/or `filters` for discovery. Filters take a record object; an unambiguous native string such as "issn:0920-8542" is also accepted when enabled and disclosed in `notice`. Native clauses split on commas outside paired double quotes and the first colon; duplicate keys and bare fragments are rejected. Any filter value sent unquoted must have paired double quotes; balanced search phrases remain valid. Supports keyword search with boolean operators, exact phrase matching, AI semantic search, and seeded random samples. Use openalex_resolve_name to resolve names to IDs before filtering. Searches and ID lookups return a curated set of fields by default; pass `select` to override with specific fields, or `["*"]` for the full record. A page holds `per_page` records and `next_cursor` continues it — semantic search and a seeded `sample` continue with `page` instead; an `id` lookup returns every selected array whole, and `slice` pages one array by count.

entity_type.description: Type of scholarly entity to search.

id.description: Retrieve a single entity by ID. Supports: OpenAlex ID ("W2741809807", or its OpenAlex record-page or API URL such as "https://openalex.org/works/W2741809807" or "https://api.openalex.org/works/W2741809807"), whose letter must name `entity_type` — W works, A authors, S sources, I institutions, T topics, P publishers, F funders, G awards; DOI ("10.1038/nature12373"; under entity_type "funders", a funder's Crossref Funder Registry DOI such as "10.13039/100000001"), ORCID ("0000-0002-1825-0097"), ROR ("https://ror.org/00hx57361" — one ROR can name an institution, a funder, and a publisher, and `entity_type` picks which), PMID ("12345678" or "https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/12345678"), ISSN ("1234-5678"). Keywords are identified by slug rather than a native ID — pass either the slug ("groundwater") or the URL a search returns ("https://openalex.org/keywords/groundwater"). A PMCID is recognized too, bare ("PMC1234567") or as a PubMed Central URL, but OpenAlex indexes no PMCIDs, so it resolves nothing — pass the work's PMID or DOI instead. When provided, `query`, `search_mode`, `filters`, `sort`, `sample`, and `seed` are not applied — the returned record is the entity at that ID regardless of them, and the response `notice` names any you passed. `select` still applies: the curated per-entity-type default is returned unless you pass `select` (use `["*"]` for the complete record). Every selected array returns whole; `slice` pages a long one by count. To filter, drop `id` and search. Use openalex_resolve_name to find the ID if unknown.

query.description: Text search query. Supports boolean operators (AND, OR, NOT), quoted phrases ("exact match"), wildcards (machin*), fuzzy matching (machin~1), and proximity ("climate change"~5). Omit for filter-only queries — an empty string is rejected, since a blank search is a mistake rather than a request for the whole catalog.

search_mode.description: Search strategy. "keyword": stemmed full-text (default). "exact": no stemming, matches individual words (use quoted phrases for multi-word exact match). "semantic": AI embedding similarity over a query-dependent candidate set whose size `meta.count` reports, at ~1 req/sec, up to 50 per page, and paginated with `page` rather than `cursor`.

filters.description: Filter criteria as field:value pairs. AND across fields (multiple keys). OR within field: pipe-separate ("us|gb"). NOT: prefix "!" ("!us"). Range: "2020-2024". Comparison: ">100", "<50". AND within same field: "+"-separate ("us+gb"); inside a `.search` value, a DOI, a date (a timestamp's "+00:00" offset), a URL field such as landing_page_url, an exactly matched name (display_name, awards.funder_display_name — "C++", "Erasmus+"), a biblio field (issue "1+2"), or awards.funder_award_id, "+" is a literal character. A value cannot mix "|" with an AND operator — a "+", or a space between values on an ID, code, or `language` key (a space inside a language name is part of the name, and a country field never reads a space as AND) — OpenAlex splits it on "|" first and drops every alternative that ANDs more than one value, so such a value is rejected; put the AND in a second key instead ("institutions.country_code": "US" beside "authorships.institutions.country_code": "DE|FR" on works). On a field matched as whole text (display_name, awards.funder_display_name, awards.funder_award_id, geo.city, geo.region, raw_affiliation_strings, block_key, biblio fields), a space is part of the value: "New York", "!New York", and "New York|Boston" match as written, but quotes around one "|" alternative make that alternative match nothing. A comma is part of such a value too ("University of California, Berkeley" on raw_affiliation_strings): a value holding one is sent as one quoted phrase, its "+" a literal character. A value sent as a quoted phrase cannot contain a double quote of its own. A multi-word value there cannot be ANDed with another ("New York+Boston" matches nothing); to require two funders or institutions, AND their IDs (awards.funder_id, authorships.institutions.id). Country fields (keys ending in country_code, country_codes, or countries) take ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 codes ("DE"): an alpha-3 code ("DEU"), numeric code ("276"), or English name ("Germany", "South Korea") is converted, "UK" becomes "GB", and a value that cannot be a country code is rejected. A space there is part of a name, never a separator: "South Korea|Japan" ORs two countries, and "DE US" is rejected. `language` takes ISO 639-1 codes ("en"): an ISO 639-2 code ("eng") or English name ("English") is converted. Two keys that resolve to the same upstream field (an alias and its canonical name, e.g. `year` and `publication_year`) are both applied and AND'd, so they narrow rather than override each other. Use OpenAlex IDs (not names) for entity filters — resolve names first. Common keys: `openalex` (filter by entity ID, e.g. {"openalex": "W123|W456"}), `cites` (works citing a given work), `publication_year` (range "2020-2024"), `authorships.author.id`, `type`, `is_oa`.

sort.description: Sort field. Prefix with "-" for descending. Comma-separate for a multi-key sort, applied left to right, with the "-" prefix set per key ("-publication_year,cited_by_count" sorts by year descending, then citations ascending). Common: "cited_by_count", "-publication_date", "-relevance_score" (default when query present). Note: when combined with a keyword query, an explicit sort overrides relevance ranking entirely — top results may be highly cited but only tangentially on-topic. Use "-relevance_score" or omit sort to keep the most relevant results first. "-relevance_score" requires an active search via "query" or a "filter:search" filter — passing it without one will fail. Not combinable with `sample` — a search passing both is rejected.

select.description: OpenAlex top-level field names to return. Always returned: `id`, `display_name` — additional fields you list are appended. A curated default per entity type applies to both searches and single-entity (`id`) lookups; pass field names to override it, or `["*"]` to retrieve the complete record (every field). Only top-level fields project, so a nested value is requested by its parent object: bibliometrics (`h_index`, `i10_index`, `2yr_mean_citedness`) live under `summary_stats` on authors, sources, institutions, publishers, and funders, and naming a leaf returns that object. On sources, `publisher` returns `host_organization_name`: the publisher of a journal, the hosting institution of a repository, and null on most sources. On works, `author_list` returns each author in authorship order as `{id, display_name, orcid}` (`orcid` null when absent), a compact alternative to `authorships`, which also carries institutions and affiliations; neither the default nor `["*"]` includes it. Invalid field names produce an error identifying the rejected field. A wide projection on a large page makes a large response, so name the fields you need. Not applied with `slice`. Example: ["doi", "author_list", "primary_topic"].

per_page.description: Results per page. Default 25, or under `sample` the sample size up to 100, so a sample of 100 or fewer returns whole in one call. A larger value returns at most 100 and says so — at most 50 under search_mode "semantic", which OpenAlex also limits to about 1 request per second. A server set to OPENALEX_CLAMP_PER_PAGE=false rejects a value over either cap instead. An `id` lookup ignores page size.

cursor.description: Pagination cursor from a previous response. Pass to get the next page. Omit it on the first call — an empty string is rejected, since a supplied-but-blank cursor is a caller mistake rather than a request for page 1. Keyword and exact modes only — semantic search walks its candidates with `page`, and a `cursor` sent with it is rejected.

page.description: Page number (1-based) for semantic search and for a seeded `sample`, the two searches that paginate with `page` instead of `cursor`. Semantic search ranks a query-dependent candidate set whose size `meta.count` reports, so the last reachable page is ceil(meta.count / per_page) — e.g. page 14 for a count of 70 with per_page=5. Passing it with any other search is rejected.

sample.description: Return a random sample of this many entities matching the filters, up to 10,000; a larger value draws 10,000 and says so (rejected instead on a server set to OPENALEX_CLAMP_PER_PAGE=false). The sample comes back `per_page` records at a time — by default the whole sample up to 100 — and a larger one is walked with `page` and a `seed`, which fixes the draw; without `seed` only its first page is returned. `meta.count` stays the population matching the filters. Cannot be combined with `cursor` or `sort` — a sample has no order, and a search passing either is rejected. Useful for unbiased exploration: spot-checking filter correctness, stratified review prompts, or generating exploration sets without bias toward most-cited.

seed.description: Deterministic seed for `sample`. Same seed + same filters = the same draw, page for page — required to walk a sample larger than one page with `page`, and worth passing whenever reproducibility matters. Has no effect without `sample`, and a search that passes it alone is rejected.

slice.description: Page one array of the record at `id`: returns `id`, `display_name`, and `limit` elements of `field` from `offset` — fewer only at the array end — with the window in `windows`, whose `next` call repeats `limit` from the following offset. Requires `id`; replaces `select`. An offset at or past the end returns an empty window. A 100-author list cap can be continued on the singleton; at 5,000 stored authors the byline remains possibly capped, but `next` is null once stored entries are exhausted.

field.description: Top-level array field to page, such as "authorships", "author_list", or "referenced_works". Leave it empty to skip slicing.

offset.description: 0-based index of the first element to return.

limit.description: Elements to return. Default 50; a larger value returns at most 5,000 and says so (rejected instead on a server set to OPENALEX_CLAMP_PER_PAGE=false).

count.description: Total results matching the query/filters — under `sample` too, whose draw holds min(sample, count) records. Under search_mode "semantic" it is instead the size of the ranked candidate set — the most results `page` can reach — not an exhaustive match total.

per_page.description: Page size OpenAlex echoed for this request — the applied per_page after clamping or its default, not the number of records returned. A singleton reports 1. A short or exhausted page carries fewer records than this.

next_cursor.description: Cursor for the next page; pass it back unchanged as `cursor`. null when no further page exists — always under semantic search and `sample`, which continue with `page` — except on a final page that exactly fills `per_page`: OpenAlex still returns a cursor there, and it leads to an empty page.

id.description: OpenAlex ID URL (e.g., "https://openalex.org/W2741809807"). `windows` names records by the bare ID ("W2741809807"); a keyword keeps its URL.

display_name.description: Entity name or work title. null when OpenAlex holds no title for the record (paratext works and other untitled entries) — use `id` to identify it.

items.description: A single OpenAlex entity record. `id` is always present and `display_name` is always returned (though it may be null); additional fields vary by entity_type and `select`.

results.description: OpenAlex entity objects. Text values are plain text — HTML entities decoded, HTML/JATS/MathML markup removed — except identifier and URL fields such as `id`, `doi`, `ids`, and `*_url`, returned exactly as OpenAlex stores them; an abstract arrives reconstructed as `abstract`, and a selected `author_list` as one `{id, display_name, orcid}` entry per author. Additional fields depend on entity_type and select. Possibly capped author arrays and `slice` windows are in `windows`.

windows.description: Author arrays possibly capped at 100 on a list record or 5,000 stored on a singleton, and the window of every `slice` call — present even when the slice holds the whole array. A slice window's `next` repeats its `slice.limit` from the following offset; `next` is null at the stored-array end, including a possibly capped singleton.

id.description: Bare ID of the record.

offset.description: Index of the first element shown.

total.description: Stored array length returned to this call, not a complete byline total.

possibly_capped.description: True for exactly 100 authorships or author_list entries on a list record, or 5,000 on a singleton lookup: the byline may be longer than the returned array.

next.description: `id` + `slice` call for the next elements; null at the array end.

items.description: An array returned in part, or possibly in part.

echo.description: Compact echo of the criteria that actually ran (entity_type, query, filters, sort, search_mode) — surfaces what was searched when results are empty. An `id` lookup echoes entity_type and id alone, because the search criteria are not applied on that path.

totalCount.description: Total results matching the query/filters across all pages.

notice.description: Guidance notice. Set when per_page, sample, or slice.limit was clamped (requested and applied sizes), a native filter string was converted, a first call has no matches, a continuation is exhausted, an id lookup ignores search criteria, semantic search reports a candidate total and whether a later `page` holds more, a sample draws more than one page (the next `page`, its last page, or that `seed` makes it pageable), an author array is possibly capped (100 list entries or 5,000 stored singleton entries), a slice offset is past the end, or slice replaces select. Absent otherwise.

costUsd.description: USD this call spent. 0 for an `id` lookup by an OpenAlex ID, DOI, ORCID, ROR, PMID, or ISSN — OpenAlex does not bill those single-entity fetches, so batching known IDs beats paging a filtered list. OpenAlex bills like one list request a keyword looked up by its slug, an `id` carrying characters past the identifier itself (`W2741809807#x` still returns W2741809807), and a funder looked up by its Funder Registry DOI.

remainingUsd.description: USD left in today's OpenAlex budget after this call.

resetsInSeconds.description: Seconds until the daily budget refills (midnight UTC).

prepaidRemainingUsd.description: USD left in the prepaid balance — a separate pool OpenAlex draws on only after the daily allowance runs out, and which the daily reset does not refill. Add it to `remainingUsd` for the full spendable amount. Absent when the account holds no prepaid balance.

error.description: Present when the call failed. Absent on success.

code.description: JSON-RPC error code for this failure.

message.description: Human-readable description of what went wrong.

"semantic" and supplied `cursor`, which OpenAlex rejects on a semantic query. `page_without_semantic`: A search supplied `page` with neither search_mode "semantic" nor `sample`. `sample_with_cursor`: A search (no `id`) provided both `sample` and `cursor`. `sample_page_without_seed`: A search (no `id`) provided `page` with `sample` but no `seed`, which OpenAlex refuses: an unseeded sample redraws on every call, so its pages would overlap. `sample_page_too_deep`: A sample page reaches past record 10,000 (`page` × `per_page` above 10,000), the most of a sample OpenAlex serves by page number. `sample_with_semantic`: A search (no `id`) provided `sample` with search_mode "semantic", which OpenAlex does not sample — it returns the same ranked candidates under every seed. `sample_with_sort`: A search (no `id`) provided both `sample` and `sort`, which OpenAlex refuses together. `seed_without_sample`: A search (no `id`) provided `seed` without `sample`. `slice_without_id`: A search passed `slice` without `id` — slice pages one array of one record. `slice_field_not_array`: The `slice` field is `*`, or is not an array on the record at `id` — absent, null, a scalar, or an object. `id_type_mismatch`: `id` is a native OpenAlex ID whose letter names another entity type than `entity_type`, or a concept ID (C…), a type this server does not serve. `id_dot_segment`: `id` holds a `.` or `..` path segment, written plainly or percent-encoded. `entity_not_found`: Lookup by id matched no OpenAlex entity. `rate_limited`: OpenAlex throttled the request for exceeding its per-second ceiling (HTTP 429). `upstream_budget_exhausted`: The OpenAlex daily usage budget is spent (HTTP 429). `upstream_plan_required`: A filter is one OpenAlex serves only on a paid plan — created_date, updated_date, or a from_/to_ form of either (HTTP 429 "Plan upgrade required"). `upstream_timeout`: OpenAlex did not respond within the request deadline. `upstream_unavailable`: OpenAlex was unreachable or unusable — HTTP 503, a connection failure, a body that was empty, HTML, or unparseable JSON, or a semantic search whose query embedding failed upstream (HTTP 400 `Failed to embed definition.name: openalex__openalex_analyze_trends_9c46fe8c
definition.title: Openalex Analyze Trends
definition.description: Aggregate OpenAlex entities into groups and count them. Use for trend analysis (group works by publication_year), distribution analysis (group by oa_status, type, country), and comparative analysis (group by institution or topic). Combine with filters to scope the analysis. Returns up to 200 groups per page — use order "key" and cursor pagination for fields with many distinct values. OpenAlex can wrap a key-ordered walk to earlier groups. Stop when a page's first key repeats an earlier key, or when a page is short or empty.

group_by.description: Field to group by. Works examples: "publication_year", "type", "oa_status", "primary_topic.field.id", "authorships.institutions.country_code", "is_retracted". The native ":include_unknown" suffix also enables include_unknown, even when the boolean is false; passing both adds the suffix once. OpenAlex builds authorships.countries groups from only the first 100 authorships of each work; authorships.institutions.country_code counts every authorship. Authors: "last_known_institutions.country_code", "has_orcid". Sources: "type", "is_oa", "country_code". Awards: "start_year", "funder.id", "funding_type" — groups count awards and do not sum amount_usd. Not all fields support group_by — call openalex_describe_fields(entity_type, "group_by") for the groupable set.

filters.description: Filter record object, using the same value syntax as openalex_search_entities; native string input is unavailable here. Narrows the population before aggregation. Country fields take ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 codes ("DE") and `language` takes ISO 639-1 codes ("en"); alpha-3, numeric, ISO 639-2, and English-name forms are converted — a multi-word name is one value, so "South Korea|Japan" ORs two countries — and a value that cannot be a country code is rejected. A multi-word value on a field matched as whole text (display_name, awards.funder_display_name, geo.city, raw_affiliation_strings) matches as one phrase ("National Science Foundation"; a comma, as in "University of California, Berkeley", is part of it, and it cannot contain a double quote of its own), "!" and "|" included, but cannot be ANDed with "+" in the same field. A value sent unquoted must have paired double quotes; balanced search phrases remain valid. A value mixing "|" with an AND operator — a "+", or a space on a field where words mean AND — is rejected, since OpenAlex drops every "|" alternative that ANDs more than one value; put the AND in a second key instead. For full-text within filters, use abstract.search, title.search, or default.search — there is no bare 'search' filter key. Example: group works by year filtered to a specific topic.

include_unknown.description: Add a group for entities with no value for the grouped field. Hidden by default unless group_by has the native ":include_unknown" suffix, which enables this setting even when the boolean is false; passing both adds the suffix once. That group carries `is_unknown: true`; OpenAlex keys it -111 or -111.0 on numeric fields, "unknown" on text fields and under order "key", and an ID ending in /unknown on ID fields — a sentinel, not a measured value. The key is not a filter value: passing -111 as a filter matches a numeric range, not the entities with no value. Boolean fields have no separate group — a missing value counts as false.

per_page.description: Maximum groups per page. Default 200 (the upstream cap); positive integers above 200 clamp to 200 with a notice unless OPENALEX_CLAMP_PER_PAGE=false restores rejection. A real top-N knob in count order without a cursor (the default) — reduce to return only the highest-count groups.

order.description: Sort order for groups. Without a cursor, omit or pass "count" (default) to return the top-N groups by count descending — no further pages. Pass "key" to enumerate distinct values in key-ascending order with cursor pagination. Boolean fields keep count order even with "key" and do not support cursor pagination. A supplied cursor selects key order even if order is omitted or "count". OpenAlex can wrap a key-ordered walk to earlier groups. Stop when a page's first key repeats an earlier key, or when a page is short or empty.

cursor.description: Pagination cursor from a previous response. A supplied cursor selects key order even if order is omitted or "count". Pass the next_cursor from the previous response to advance, subject to the stop conditions below. Omit it on the first call — an empty string is rejected, since a supplied-but-blank cursor is a caller mistake rather than a request for the first page. OpenAlex can wrap a key-ordered walk to earlier groups. Stop when a page's first key repeats an earlier key, or when a page is short or empty.

count.description: Total entities matching the filters (before grouping).

groups_count.description: Number of groups on this page (max 200).

next_cursor.description: Upstream continuation cursor; null when OpenAlex supplies none. A non-null cursor does not guarantee unseen groups. OpenAlex can wrap a key-ordered walk to earlier groups. Stop when a page's first key repeats an earlier key, or when a page is short or empty.

key.description: Group key (OpenAlex ID or raw value), exactly as OpenAlex returns it.

key_display_name.description: Human-readable group label as plain text, with HTML entities decoded and markup removed; null when OpenAlex supplies no label. Text output uses the group key when the label is null.

count.description: Number of entities in this group.

is_unknown.description: Present only on the group include_unknown adds for entities with no value; its key is an OpenAlex sentinel (-111, -111.0, unknown, or an ID ending in /unknown), not a measured value.

items.description: A single aggregation group with its key, display label, and entity count.

echo.description: Compact echo of the criteria (entity_type, group_by, filters) and effective include_unknown and order settings — surfaces what was actually requested when no groups are returned.

totalCount.description: Total entities matching the filters before grouping (across all pages).

notice.description: Guidance notice. Set when per_page was clamped (requested and applied sizes), on every effective key-order call (upstream wrap warning and stopping conditions), when a first call returns no groups (recovery suggestions), when a cursor continuation returns none because the traversal is already finished, when a count-order page is full and more groups likely exist (truncation signal with narrowing advice), or when works are grouped by authorships.countries, which OpenAlex counts from only the first 100 authorships of each work. Absent otherwise.

budget.description: What this call cost against the OpenAlex daily budget and what is left of it — weigh `remainingUsd` against `costUsd` before enumerating every group with `order: "key"`. Absent when OpenAlex omitted the accounting headers.

costUsd.description: USD this call spent. Aggregation is priced far below paging the same entities, so a group_by is the cheap way to size a population before searching it.

remainingUsd.description: USD left in today's OpenAlex budget after this call.

resetsInSeconds.description: Seconds until the daily budget refills (midnight UTC).

prepaidRemainingUsd.description: USD left in the prepaid balance — a separate pool OpenAlex draws on only after the daily allowance runs out, and which the daily reset does not refill. Add it to `remainingUsd` for the full spendable amount. Absent when the account holds no prepaid balance.

OpenAlex splits the value on "|" first and drops every alternative that ANDs more than one value, so no single value can carry both. `quote_in_filter_value`: A filter value sent to OpenAlex double-quoted holds a double quote inside its outer pair — a value the server quotes (a multi-word value on a field matched as whole text, or a value holding a comma on such a field or on a free-text search filter), or one the caller wrapped in double quotes on any filter but a free-text search. `upstream_invalid_params`: OpenAlex rejected an invalid group_by or filter field name (HTTP 400). `upstream_invalid_id_value`: An entity-ID filter received a value that is not an OpenAlex ID — usually a name (HTTP 400). `upstream_ungroupable_group_by`: group_by targets a field OpenAlex cannot aggregate — a raw date, a decimal score, a *.search operator, a field such as display_name, doi, or referenced_works, or a concept key on authors, which OpenAlex reports as an invalid OpenAlex ID (HTTP 400). `upstream_invalid_params_other`: OpenAlex rejected the request (HTTP 400) for a reason other than an invalid field name. `upstream_validation_failed`: OpenAlex rejected the request as semantically invalid (HTTP 422). `upstream_missing_group_by`: OpenAlex answered with its plain list shape, carrying no aggregation for the requested group_by. definition.name: openalex__openalex_get_citation_graph_91ac55b8
definition.title: Openalex Get Citation Graph
definition.description: Walk the citation graph one hop from a seed work. Direction picks the edge: incoming citations (`cites`), the seed's own references (`cited_by`), or OpenAlex's algorithmically-related works (`related_to`). Note: `direction` follows OpenAlex's filter convention, which inverts the common English reading — `cites` returns works that cite the seed; `cited_by` returns works the seed cites. Results use the works schema; combine with filters/sort to narrow further. A page holds `per_page` works and `next_cursor` continues it.

seed_id.description: Seed work identifier. Accepts OpenAlex work ID ("W2741809807", or its OpenAlex record-page or API URL such as "https://openalex.org/works/W2741809807"), DOI ("10.1038/nature12373" or full URL), or PMID ("12345678" or "https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/12345678"). A PMCID is recognized too, bare or as a PubMed Central URL, but OpenAlex indexes no PMCIDs, so it resolves nothing — pass the work's PMID or DOI instead. Use openalex_resolve_name first if you only have a title.

direction.description: "cites": works that cite seed_id (incoming citations). "cited_by": works that seed_id cites (its reference list). "related_to": OpenAlex algorithmically-related works (~8-30 typical, may be empty for less-cited seeds).

filters.description: Additional filter record object to narrow the graph, using the same value syntax as openalex_search_entities; native string input is unavailable here. Example: publication_year=">2020", is_oa="true". Country fields take ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 codes ("DE") and `language` takes ISO 639-1 codes ("en"); alpha-3, numeric, ISO 639-2, and English-name forms are converted — a multi-word name is one value, so "South Korea|Japan" ORs two countries — and a value that cannot be a country code is rejected. A multi-word value on a field matched as whole text (display_name, awards.funder_display_name, authorships.institutions.geo.city, raw_affiliation_strings) matches as one phrase ("National Science Foundation"; a comma, as in "University of California, Berkeley", is part of it, and it cannot contain a double quote of its own), "!" and "|" included, but cannot be ANDed with "+" in the same field. A value sent unquoted must have paired double quotes; balanced search phrases remain valid. Filters are checked before the seed lookup. A value mixing "|" with an AND operator — a "+", or a space on a field where words mean AND — is rejected, since OpenAlex drops every "|" alternative that ANDs more than one value; put the AND in a second key instead. Do not include cites/cited_by/related_to, nor an alias of one such as cited_works — those keys are set by the `direction` parameter.

sort.description: Sort field. Prefix with "-" for descending. Comma-separate for a multi-key sort, applied left to right, with the "-" prefix set per key ("-publication_year,cited_by_count" sorts by year descending, then citations ascending). Common: "cited_by_count", "-publication_date". Default is OpenAlex relevance.

select.description: OpenAlex work field names to return. Always returned: id, display_name. Defaults to the curated works select if omitted. `author_list` returns each author in authorship order as `{id, display_name, orcid}` (`orcid` null when absent), a compact alternative to `authorships`, which also carries institutions and affiliations; neither the default nor `["*"]` includes it. A wide projection on a large page makes a large response, so name the fields you need.

per_page.description: Results per page. Default 25; a larger value returns at most 100 and says so (rejected instead on a server set to OPENALEX_CLAMP_PER_PAGE=false).

cursor.description: Pagination cursor from a previous response. Pass to get the next page. Omit it on the first call — an empty string is rejected, since a supplied-but-blank cursor is a caller mistake rather than a request for the first page.

count.description: Total edges from seed_id in this direction (across all pages).

per_page.description: Page size OpenAlex echoed for this request — the applied per_page after clamping, not the number of records returned. A short or exhausted page carries fewer records than this.

next_cursor.description: Cursor for the next page; pass it back unchanged as `cursor`. null when no further page exists, except on a final page that exactly fills `per_page`: OpenAlex still returns a cursor there, and it leads to an empty page.

id.description: OpenAlex work ID.

display_name.description: Work title. null when OpenAlex holds no title for the record (paratext works and other untitled entries) — use `id` to identify it.

items.description: A single OpenAlex work record on the citation graph. Additional fields vary by `select`.

results.description: Works on the citation graph in this direction. Text values are plain text — HTML entities decoded, HTML/JATS/MathML markup removed — except identifier and URL fields such as `id`, `doi`, `ids`, and `*_url`, returned exactly as OpenAlex stores them; an abstract arrives reconstructed as `abstract`, and a selected `author_list` as one `{id, display_name, orcid}` entry per author. Possibly capped author arrays are in `windows`.

windows.description: Author arrays possibly capped at 100 on a list record or 5,000 stored on a singleton, and the window of every `slice` call — present even when the slice holds the whole array. A slice window's `next` repeats its `slice.limit` from the following offset; `next` is null at the stored-array end, including a possibly capped singleton.

id.description: Bare ID of the record.

offset.description: Index of the first element shown.

total.description: Stored array length returned to this call, not a complete byline total.

possibly_capped.description: True for exactly 100 authorships or author_list entries on a list record, or 5,000 on a singleton lookup: the byline may be longer than the returned array.

next.description: `id` + `slice` call for the next elements; null at the array end.

items.description: An array returned in part, or possibly in part.

echo.description: Compact echo of seed_id, direction, filters, sort — surfaces what was actually queried when no edges are returned.

totalCount.description: Total edges from seed_id in this direction across all pages.

notice.description: Guidance notice. Set when per_page was clamped (requested and applied sizes), when no edges are returned — a first call suggests verifying the seed_id, broadening filters, or trying a different direction; a cursor continuation says the walk is already past its last edge — and when a work carries exactly 100 authorships or author_list entries (possibly capped). Absent otherwise.

budget.description: What this call cost against the OpenAlex daily budget and what is left of it. Price a full walk before committing to it: `totalCount` ÷ `per_page` × `costUsd` against `remainingUsd`. Absent when OpenAlex omitted the accounting headers.

costUsd.description: USD this call spent, covering both upstream requests — the seed validation lookup and the graph page itself. The seed lookup is unbilled unless seed_id carries characters past the identifier itself (`W2741809807#x` still resolves to W2741809807), which OpenAlex bills like one list request.

reason.description: Machine-readable failure mode. Declared by this tool: `unmatched_quote_in_filter_value`: A filter value sent unquoted has an unmatched double quote. `rate_limited`: OpenAlex throttled the request for exceeding its per-second ceiling (HTTP 429). `upstream_budget_exhausted`: The OpenAlex daily usage budget is spent (HTTP 429). `upstream_plan_required`: A filter is one OpenAlex serves only on a paid plan — created_date, updated_date, or a from_/to_ form of either (HTTP 429 "Plan upgrade required"). `upstream_timeout`: OpenAlex did not respond within the request deadline. `upstream_unavailable`: OpenAlex was unreachable or unusable — HTTP 503, a connection failure, or a body that was empty, HTML, or unparseable JSON. `upstream_unauthorized`: OpenAlex rejected the API key (HTTP 401). `upstream_forbidden`: OpenAlex denied access to the requested resource (HTTP 403). `comma_in_filter_value`: A filter value contains a comma, which collides with the OpenAlex filter separator, on a field that takes no phrase. Free-text search filters (any `.search` key, such as title.search or abstract.search.exact) and fields matched as whole text (display_name, awards.funder_display_name, awards.funder_award_id, authorships.institutions.geo.city, authorships.institutions.geo.region, raw_affiliation_strings, biblio fields) are exempt: a comma there is sent quoted, as part of the phrase. `invalid_country_code`: A country filter (a key ending in country_code, country_codes, or countries) holds a segment that cannot be a country code, such as a misspelled name, an unassigned number, "unknown", or two codes joined by a space ("DE US"). `mixed_and_or_in_filter_value`: A filter value puts "|" (OR) beside an AND operator — a "+", or a space on a field where words mean AND (on a country field a space is always part of a country name, and inside a language name it is part of the name). OpenAlex splits the value on "|" first and drops every alternative that ANDs more than one value, so no single value can carry both. `quote_in_filter_value`: A filter value sent to OpenAlex double-quoted holds a double quote inside its outer pair — a value the server quotes (a multi-word value on a field matched as whole text, or a value holding a comma on such a field or on a free-text search filter), or one the caller wrapped in double quotes on any filter but a free-text search. `upstream_invalid_params`: OpenAlex rejected an invalid filter, select, or sort field name (HTTP 400). `upstream_invalid_id_value`: An entity-ID filter received a value that is not an OpenAlex ID — usually a name (HTTP 400). `upstream_sort_requires_search`: sort=-relevance_score was used but the citation-graph query has no active search (HTTP 400). `upstream_invalid_params_other`: OpenAlex rejected the request (HTTP 400) for a reason other than an invalid field name. `reserved_filter_key`: filters contains cites/cited_by/related_to, or an alias of one such as cited_works — the direction parameter reserves those keys. `id_type_mismatch`: seed_id is a native OpenAlex ID of another entity type — an author, source, institution, topic, publisher, funder, award, or concept ID rather than a work ID. `id_dot_segment`: seed_id holds a `.` or `..` path segment, written plainly or percent-encoded. `entity_not_found`: OpenAlex has no work matching the seed_id. `response_too_large`: The response's structuredContent or content[] text would exceed 8,000,000 bytes — a wide `select` on a large page. A page is never shortened to fit. Other values are possible when a failure originates below the handler.

definition.name: omnipath__execute_sql_query_on_omnipath_db_57bb922e
definition.title: Execute SQL Query on Omnipath DB
definition.description:
Execute a read-only SQL query (must start with SELECT) against the database.
Available tables and their columns:
- annotations: id, uniprot, genesymbol, entity_type, source, label, value, record_id
- complexes: id, name, components (array), components_genesymbols (array), stoichiometry, sources (array), references, identifiers
- enz_sub: id, enzyme, enzyme_genesymbol, substrate, substrate_genesymbol, isoforms, residue_type, residue_offset, modification, sources (array), references, curation_effort, ncbi_tax_id
- interactions: id, source, target, source_genesymbol, target_genesymbol, is_directed, is_stimulation, is_inhibition, consensus_direction, consensus_stimulation, consensus_inhibition, sources (array), references, omnipath, kinaseextra, ligrecextra, pathwayextra, mirnatarget, dorothea, collectri, tf_target, lncrna_mrna, tf_mirna, small_molecule, dorothea_curated, dorothea_chipseq, dorothea_tfbs, dorothea_coexp, dorothea_level (array), type, curation_effort, extra_attrs (jsonb), evidences (jsonb), ncbi_tax_id_source, entity_type_source, ncbi_tax_id_target, entity_type_target
- intercell: id, category, parent, database, scope, aspect, source, uniprot, genesymbol, entity_type, consensus_score, transmitter, receiver, secreted, plasma_membrane_transmembrane, plasma_membrane_peripheral
- uniprot_identifiers: id, uniprot_accession, identifier_type, identifier_value

Example queries:
• Canonical pathways for a protein:
  SELECT * FROM annotations WHERE source IN ('SignaLink_pathway', 'SIGNOR', 'NetPath', 'KEGG-PC') AND (uniprot = '<uniprot_accession>' OR genesymbol = '<genesymbol>')

• Find transcription factor regulators:
  SELECT * FROM interactions WHERE collectri AND (target = '<uniprot_accession>' OR target_genesymbol = '<genesymbol>')

• Find TF suppressors (inhibitors):
  SELECT * FROM interactions WHERE collectri AND (target = '<uniprot_accession>' OR target_genesymbol = '<genesymbol>') AND is_inhibition = TRUE

• Check if protein is a transcription factor:
  SELECT * FROM annotations WHERE source = 'TFcensus' AND value = 'a' AND (uniprot = '<uniprot_accession>' OR genesymbol = '<genesymbol>')

• Find ligands of a receptor:
  SELECT source_genesymbol FROM interactions WHERE ligrecextra AND (target = '<uniprot_accession>' OR target_genesymbol = '<genesymbol>')

• Basic interaction query:
  SELECT source_genesymbol, target_genesymbol, type FROM interactions WHERE source_genesymbol = 'EGFR'

sqlQuery.description: The read-only SQL query (starting with SELECT) to execute.

definition.name: medical__icd11_lookup_4484f120
definition.title: ICD-11 Entity Details
definition.description:
Get detailed information about ONE ICD-11 entity you already have a code or URI for.

Use this tool to:
- Get the full definition of a disease
- Retrieve coding notes, inclusions and exclusions
- Get the official title and index terms (synonyms)

Provide `code` (e.g., "BA00") or `uri` (any URI a previous answer returned) — at least one is required; calling with neither returns a validation error naming both. Set `language` for WHO's official translations (e.g. `language: "pt"` for official Portuguese).

Returns a single entity (no pagination). A code WHO does not know comes back as a "not found" error, never an empty record.

When NOT to use: to find a code from a disease name, use icd11_search first; to walk parents/children, use icd11_hierarchy; for an ICD-10 code (like "E11"), convert it with map_icd10_to_icd11 — ICD-10 codes are not ICD-11 codes.

definition.name: medical__icd11_hierarchy_50e29f6b
definition.title: Browse ICD-11 Hierarchy
definition.description:
Navigate the ICD-11 hierarchy to find parent or child entities.

Use this tool to:
- Find broader categories (parents) of a condition
- Find specific subtypes (children) of a condition
- Understand the classification structure

definition.name: medical__icd11_chapters_54489032
definition.title: List ICD-11 Chapters
definition.description:
List all ICD-11 chapters (top-level categories) of the pinned WHO release.

Use this tool to:
- Get an overview of ICD-11 structure
- Find which chapter covers a body system or condition type
- Get chapter URIs to drill down with icd11_hierarchy (direction 'children')

Returns 28 entries in one response, no pagination — chapters 01-26 plus the supplementary sections V (functioning) and X (extension codes) — each with number, code, title and URI. Each chapter is fetched separately from WHO; if one fetch fails, that entry keeps its URI and carries an `error` instead of a title, and the rest still come back. Set `language` for WHO's official translations (e.g. `language: "pt"`); the result is cached, so repeated calls are cheap.

When NOT to use: to find a specific disease, use icd11_search; for the Brazilian CID-10 (ICD-10) chapters, use cid10_chapters.

definition.name: medical__icd11_postcoordination_2950b39b
definition.title: ICD-11 Postcoordination Options
definition.description:
List the postcoordination axes WHO allows for one ICD-11 stem code (MMS linearization, pinned release).

Postcoordination means attaching extra detail to a stem code — severity, laterality, anatomy, causing agent, etc. — to build a composite (cluster) code.

Use this tool to:
- See which axes a stem code accepts before building a composite code
- Check which axes are REQUIRED vs optional
- See whether an axis takes one or several values, and how many values it offers

Provide an ICD-11 `code` (e.g., "BA00"). Returns one entry per axis with `axis_name`, `required`, `allow_multiple` and `value_count` — the count of allowed values, not the values themselves. A code with no postcoordination, or one WHO does not know, returns an empty `axes` list (not an error), so check the code with icd11_lookup if the list is unexpectedly empty.

When NOT to use: this does not build or validate a composite code, and it does not list the allowed values; to get a code from a disease name, use icd11_search.

code.description: ICD-11 code to get postcoordination info for
The ICD-11 code as submitted.

axes.description: Postcoordination axes the WHO allows for this code; empty when it has none or the WHO has no postcoordination info for it.

definition.name: medical__map_icd10_to_icd11_ad0ee0fa
definition.title: Map ICD-10 to ICD-11
definition.description:
Authoritative ICD-10 → ICD-11 mapping using WHO transition tables (release 2025-01, bundled with the server).

Returns the primary 1:1 ICD-11 category for the ICD-10 code plus any alternative ICD-11 candidates that WHO documents (some ICD-10 concepts split into multiple ICD-11 entities). For each mapping, includes the ICD-11 code, title, chapter, and the Foundation URI / Linearization URI for navigating to the full entity definition.

Use this for clinical coding, billing migration, retrospective analysis, and any workflow that needs authoritative mapping rather than text-search candidates. Coverage: 11,243 ICD-10 categories (excludes chapters and blocks like "A00-A09" which aren't used in clinical coding).

Provide a code like "E11" (Type 2 diabetes), "I21" (Acute MI), or "A07.8" (4 alternatives in WHO's table). Both dotted ("A07.8") and undotted ("A078") forms are accepted.

Returns "no mapping" when the code isn't in the WHO category-level table — that's the honest answer rather than a fuzzy search fallback.

definition.name: medical__validate_codes_61d7d887
definition.title: Validate Medical Codes
definition.description:
Validate a mixed batch of medical codes against their source terminologies. Useful for retrospective analysis of legacy databases — flag codes that no longer exist, surface ICD-10 → ICD-11 replacements, and grade activity status where the terminology exposes it.

For each input `{ code, terminology }`, returns:
- **valid**: whether the code exists in the source terminology.
- **active**: whether the code is currently active. Null when the source doesn't expose an explicit active/inactive distinction at category level (CID-10, ATC, ICD-11, RxNorm, MeSH all return null today; LOINC returns a real boolean).
- **title**: the official label/name when available.
- **replaced_by**: a successor code, populated today only for ICD-10 codes that have a primary ICD-11 mapping in the bundled WHO transition tables.
- **source**: human-readable provenance of the validation (terminology + release/version).
- **error**: non-null only when validation couldn't be performed (network error, upstream outage, etc.). `valid: false` + `error: null` means "code not found"; `valid: false` + `error: set` means "couldn't validate".

Terminology is **required per code** — auto-detection isn't supported because category codes like "A00" exist in both ICD-10 and CID-10. Accepted values: `icd11`, `icd10`, `loinc`, `rxnorm`, `mesh`, `atc`, `cid10`.

Hard cap of 50 codes per call; codes are validated in parallel through their respective clients, so total wall time scales with the slowest upstream + its rate limit (worst case ~10 s for a full batch hitting ICD-11).

definition.name: medical__find_equivalent_221654f0
definition.title: Find Equivalents Across Terminologies
definition.description:
Ranked unified search for equivalent terms across multiple medical terminologies.

Use this tool to:
- Find the same concept in different coding systems
- Compare how terminologies represent a concept
- Support terminology mapping and data integration

Searches across: ICD-11, LOINC, RxNorm, and MeSH. Set `target_terminologies` to limit which are searched, or set `source_terminology` to exclude one (e.g. when you already have a code from that terminology and want equivalents elsewhere). The two combine: source is subtracted from targets. `limit` caps candidates per terminology (default 5, max 10).

Every candidate carries `match_score` (lexical similarity to the search term, 0-1) and `rank` (global position across all searched terminologies) — both computed by this server, since upstreams don't expose comparable relevance scores. Candidates from different terminologies whose titles are lexically identical are clustered in `groups` — a strong same-concept signal (absence of a group is NOT evidence of non-equivalence).

Searches upstreams in English. For official pt-BR content, use the dedicated tools: `icd11_search`/`mesh_search` accept `language: "pt"`, and `cid10_search` is natively Portuguese.

definition.name: medical__harmonize_terms_df67230f
definition.title: Harmonize Free-Text Terms to Standard Codes
definition.description:
Map a LIST of free-text clinical terms to standard codes in one call, with ranked candidates and a confidence label for each — the building block of a reviewable crosswalk.

Use this tool to:
- Harmonize a column of diagnoses, drugs or lab names from a dataset to ICD-11 / RxNorm (+ ATC) / LOINC
- Triage which terms map cleanly (exact / strong) and which need a person (needs_review)
- Build a crosswalk you can audit: every row keeps its candidates, scores and sources

Give each term its `domain`: diagnosis → ICD-11; drug → RxNorm concepts (ingredients first) plus the ATC classes of the term; lab → LOINC. Up to 50 terms per call — a longer list is refused with a validation error: split it into batches of 50. Repeated term+domain pairs are looked up once. `max_candidates` keeps 1-5 per term (default 3).

Every candidate carries `match_score` (lexical, 0-1, the find_equivalent formula) and `match_type`: exact = same words after normalization; strong = every term word is in the title (or the matched synonym) and score ≥ 0.85; needs_review = anything else. A one-word term is exact or needs_review, never strong ("Tylenol" vs "Tylenol PM" is a different product). Synonyms, abbreviations ("MI", "HbA1c") and misspellings land in needs_review or no_candidates — the label errs toward asking a person. Candidates sharing no word with the term are dropped, as are LOINC codes named "Deprecated". For diagnoses, a candidate is also scored against the synonyms WHO matched (e.g. "hypertension NOS" for Essential hypertension), reported in `matched_label`; postcoordinated clusters (codes with "/" or "&") are left out — build those with icd11_postcoordination. Lab names are ambiguous without specimen and property: "glucose" matches over a thousand LOINC codes, so write "glucose serum" or expect needs_review. One failed lookup does not fail the batch: that row comes back with status "error".

Terms are searched in English and sent to the WHO and NLM APIs — de-identify the list first. For Brazilian Portuguese diagnoses use cid10_search; to check codes you already have, use validate_codes; for one term across every terminology, use find_equivalent. Record the vocabulary versions with the provenance blocks (one per source) and terminology_versions.

terms.description: Terms to harmonize, each with its domain. Up to 50 per call; repeated term+domain pairs are looked up once.

definition.name: medical__atc_classify_90a40a21
definition.title: ATC Classification for a Drug
definition.description:
Look up the WHO ATC (Anatomical Therapeutic Chemical) classification(s) for a drug by name.

Use this tool to:
- Find the ATC code for a medication (e.g., "metformin" → A10BA02)
- Identify the therapeutic and pharmacological class hierarchy
- Cross-reference drugs with their international ATC codes

Returns one entry per ATC code the drug belongs to. A single-ingredient drug typically maps to one substance-level code; combination products map to multiple. ATC codes are international (WHO Collaborating Centre); this tool retrieves them via NLM RxClass.

Input is a drug NAME (brand or generic, English/US naming as in RxNorm). A name RxNorm does not recognize, or a drug without an ATC mapping, returns an empty `matches` list with an explanatory note — not an error; try the generic name, or resolve the name first with rxnorm_search.

Which ATC tool: start here when you have a drug name; use atc_lookup when you already have a class code (level 1-4, e.g. "A10BA") and want its name; use atc_members to list the drugs inside a class.

definition.name: medical__cid10_search_82eb5fbd
definition.title: Buscar na CID-10
definition.description:
Search the Brazilian CID-10 (Classificação Estatística Internacional de Doenças, 10ª Revisão) by Portuguese text.

Use this tool to:
- Find CID-10 codes for Brazilian SUS / ANVISA contexts ("infarto", "diabetes", "tuberculose")
- Look up the official Portuguese (CBCD/USP) translation of a clinical term
- Locate codes for billing, epidemiology, and clinical documentation in Brazil

Returns matches from CID-10 categories (3-char) and/or subcategories (4-char). Search is diacritic-insensitive: typing "infeccoes" matches "infecções". Every word must match (AND), and everyday Portuguese is resolved to the CID-10's own wording (câncer→neoplasia maligna, AVC→acidente vascular cerebral, pressão alta→hipertensão, suicídio→lesão autoprovocada, aids→HIV); when that happens the response says so in vocabulary_notes. This tool searches the Brazilian Portuguese CID-10 V2008 — for the international ICD-11 (current WHO revision, in English by default), use icd11_search.

definition.title: Capítulo da CID-10
definition.description:

Which CID-10 tool: use cid10_chapters first if you do not know the chapter number (it lists all 22 with code ranges); use cid10_lookup for one specific code and cid10_search to find codes by Portuguese text. For the international ICD-11, use icd11_chapters.
