vwap_fill_price.description: Single-market mode: volume-weighted fill price across the requested size; null if nothing filled.

slippage_pp.description: Single-market mode: |vwap - top_of_book| in percentage points.

shares_filled.description: Single-market mode: shares actually fillable from visible depth.

usd_filled.description: Single-market mode: dollars actually fillable from visible depth.

max_fillable_usd.description: Single-market mode: total USD value of the entire visible side of the book.

book_levels_visible.description: Single-market mode: count of price levels on the side priced.

fee_schedule.description: Polymarket's published taker-fee parameters for this market, read off the market payload (fleet #3446) — never assumed fee-free.

taker_rate.description: Taker-fee rate actually applied (0 means genuinely fee-free, never "unknown").

exponent.description: Exponent in fee = shares × rate × (p×(1-p))^exponent — 1 on every market observed.

maker_rebate_rate.description: Polymarket's published maker rebate rate, when known.

fees_enabled.description: false means this market genuinely charges no taker fee.

basis.description: Where the rate came from — payload (read off this market) is the most trustworthy.

fee_usd.description: Single-market mode: Polymarket taker fee in USD on the shares actually filled.

fee_pp.description: Single-market mode: the taker fee as a percentage point of a $1 share — size-invariant, so it's the same number at any trade size.

breakeven_win_rate_taker.description: Single-market mode: win-rate (0-1) the filled side needs to break even as a taker, INCLUDING the fee — always worse than the raw fill price.

breakeven_win_rate_maker.description: Single-market mode: win-rate a maker (no taker fee charged) would need — equals top_of_book.

all_in_cost_pp.description: Single-market mode: slippage_pp + fee_pp — the full round-trip cost of this fill.

verdict.description: Single-market mode: fill-quality verdict based on depth/slippage (independent of the fee).

reasoning.description: Plain-English explanation of the verdict, naming the all-in cost and breakeven.

strategy.description: Basket mode: which side was priced across every leg.

side_auto_selected.description: Basket mode: true if side was inferred from the partition sum rather than passed explicitly.

leg_count.description: Basket mode: number of legs priced.

truncated_legs.description: Basket mode: legs dropped by the 80-leg cap, if any.

partition_complete.description: Basket mode: false means truncated_legs > 0 — edge figures are directional only.

settlement_notional_requested_usd.description: Basket mode: requested shares-per-leg (the size_usd argument).

settlement_notional_executed_usd.description: Basket mode: shares-per-leg actually executable, scaled down by the thinnest leg.

scaled_down_by_thinnest_leg.description: Basket mode: true if executed size was capped below the requested size.

theoretical.description: Basket mode: top-of-book sum across all legs, before depth.

realizable_at_executed_size.description: Basket mode: VWAP sum across all legs at the executed size, net of each leg's own Polymarket taker fee (fleet #3446 — profit_usd was gross before).

profit_usd.description: NET of every leg's own Polymarket taker fee.

profit_usd_gross.description: Before fees — kept alongside profit_usd so the fee cost is never hidden.

fees_usd_total.description: Sum of per_leg[].fee_usd across every leg.

note.description: Present only when the basket is not executable at any size.

capture_ratio.description: Basket mode: fraction of the theoretical edge that survives depth AND fees (fleet #3446 — was gross of fees before).

capture_ratio_gross.description: Basket mode: the pre-fee figure capture_ratio used to report.

thin_legs.description: Basket mode: leg slugs that cannot cleanly absorb the requested size.

dead_legs.description: Basket mode: leg slugs with zero visible depth on the priced side.

fee_usd.description: This leg's own Polymarket taker fee in USD at the executed size.

forced_directional_risk.description: Basket mode: plain-English risk note naming dead/thin legs.

_hint.description: Usage note — what is gross vs net of fees, and what is still unmodeled.

outputSchema.description: Realizable fill risk against live order-book depth, plus Polymarket's own taker fee and the breakeven win-rate it implies (fleet #3446).

definition.name: dailymed__polymarket_edge_tracker_d45557cb
definition.title: Polymarket Edge Tracker
definition.description: Edge persistence and decay telemetry built from daily polymarket_edges snapshots. Answers "how long has this edge existed and is it shrinking?" — a fresh wide edge and a 3-week-old wide edge are different trades (the latter is wide for a reason nobody is willing to take). Args: days (lookback, default 14, max 30), window (snapshot family, default "1wk"). RESPONSE: tracked[] = every opportunity in the LATEST snapshot with its full edge_pp_net time-series across prior snapshots, first_seen, trend (new | widening | stable | decaying) and decay_pp_per_day (both computed on |edge_pp_net| — the value itself is signed by trade direction, negative = SELL YES); expired[] = opportunities that appeared in earlier snapshots but are GONE from the latest (closed, resolved, or arbed away) with their lifespan_days — the median lifespan is your competition clock; snapshot_dates[] = which days actually have data (snapshots are written when polymarket_edges runs on a cache-miss, so gaps mean nobody scanned that day). LIMITS: history depth is bounded by the 60-day snapshot TTL and starts from when snapshotting was enabled; decay numbers come from daily closes of edge_pp_net (net of default slippage AND Polymarket's own taker fee — see polymarket_edges), not intraday.

window.description: Which polymarket_edges window family to read snapshots for: 24hr | 1wk | 1mo (default 1wk).

definition.name: dailymed__kalshi_weather_edge_1260562f
definition.title: Kalshi Weather Edge
definition.description: Prices Kalshi daily high-temperature markets against the NWS forecast for the market's OWN settlement station, and measures whether that forecast actually beats the market. Two modes. LIVE (default): returns the full strike ladder for one city and settlement date with market_prob (mid), forecast_prob, and edge_pp per strike, plus the settlement clause verbatim. BACKTEST (`backtest_days: N`): scores an archived gridded forecast against the market on settled days and returns brier_market vs brier_forecast with a plain-English `verdict`, so the edge is MEASURED rather than asserted. READ THE WARNINGS — they are not boilerplate. (1) These markets DO NOT settle on the NWS. They settle on The Weather Company (weather.com) at a Kalshi station code such as CLINYC, which the response quotes verbatim; so part of every edge_pp is NWS-vs-Weather-Company disagreement about the same day at the same station, which is not mispricing and not tradeable. `settlement_vs_forecast_basis_f` from backtest mode is that part as a number. (2) The station is DERIVED from the settlement clause, never from the city name: Chicago settles at MIDWAY and New York at CENTRAL PARK, so a city-centre forecast would misprice a whole ladder. A station that cannot be resolved yields rows with no forecast and a reason, never a guessed coordinate. (3) forecast_prob assumes a normal distribution around the NWS high whose width is ASSUMED, not fitted (stated in `distribution_assumption`) — run backtest mode to see whether it is calibrated. (4) edge_pp is gross: no Kalshi fees, no bid-ask. MEASURED RESULT, AND IT IS NOT THE FLATTERING ONE: on the first backtest (KXHIGHNY, 13 settled days to 2026-09-11, 58 market observations) the MARKET beat the forecast — Brier 0.1008 for the market against 0.1594 for the archived gridded forecast, lower being better. So on that sample there is NO forecast edge to sell, and a large edge_pp is more likely to be the model disagreeing with a better-informed market than an opportunity. The measured settlement-vs-forecast basis was 1.7F mean absolute over 8 pinnable days, slightly warm-biased, which is a big share of a typical edge_pp on a 2-degree bracket. Re-run backtest_days before believing any edge; if a later sample reverses this, the numbers say so. NWS is US-only, so the ~30 international Kalshi weather series (London, Paris, Tokyo) return market prices with forecast_unavailable rather than a forecast. Precipitation series are listed but not yet priced. Cities: nyc, chicago, los angeles, miami, austin, houston, denver, philadelphia — or pass `series_ticker` for any other (e.g. "KXHIGHTBOS").

city.description: City to price, e.g. "nyc", "chicago", "los angeles", "miami", "austin", "houston", "denver", "philadelphia". Defaults to nyc. Unmapped cities return known_cities[] rather than a wrong series.

series_ticker.description: Explicit Kalshi series, e.g. "KXHIGHNY" or "KXHIGHTBOS" (Boston). Overrides `city`; use it for any of the 121 daily weather series not in the city list.

date.description: Settlement date as YYYY-MM-DD. Defaults to the soonest open event. Daily weather markets open ~1-2 days ahead and close 05:00Z the next day.

market_type.description: "high_temp" (default) | "precip". Precipitation markets return prices but no forecast_prob yet.

backtest_days.description: Run measurement mode over the last N settled days (max 60) instead of pricing today. Returns brier_market vs brier_forecast, the settlement-vs-forecast basis, and per-day detail. Both sides are scored at 12:00Z on each event day — before the daily high and before resolution — because a settled market prices the known outcome at close.

definition.name: dailymed__resolution_audit_ca6a495f
definition.title: Resolution Audit
definition.description: Extract the settlement clause of a single Polymarket (.com or .us) or Kalshi market: who publishes the settling number (source), the clock time + timezone it is taken at (falling back to the market TITLE when the clause itself says "the time range specified in the title" — e.g. Polymarket's 15-minute Chainlink TWAP family), the precision of the computation (e.g. "1-minute candle close" vs "60-second trailing average" vs "twap_60s_lookback"/"twap_30s_lookback" vs "election outcome"), comparison_basis — what is compared to what (end_average_vs_start_average | close_vs_open; orthogonal to precision, since venues can share this comparison shape while computing each endpoint differently), the evidence standard (official_source | consensus_reporting | any_credible_report | unspecified), and void_handling (cancellation/postponement settlement — reused verbatim from bet_research's cancellation_rule detector, not re-derived). Parses Polymarket's `description` field (fetched via polymarket_market, or via polymarket_us_search for the .us venue) or Kalshi's `rules_primary` + `rules_secondary` fields (fetched via kalshi_market) with regex + a small vocabulary — no LLM pass, so an unusual clause reports confidence:"low" rather than a guess. Pass `market` as a Polymarket slug/URL (either venue) or a Kalshi market ticker (e.g. "KXBTCD-26SEP1317-T66999.99"); a Kalshi EVENT ticker (e.g. "KXBTCD-26SEP1317") also works — it picks one representative market under that event, since the settlement mechanism is normally shared across all strikes/legs in one event. Use this before treating a polymarket_kalshi_spread row as a real arbitrage: two ladders that look alike can settle on different sources (Polymarket.com's Chainlink TWAP stream vs Kalshi/Polymarket US's CF Benchmarks BRTI), at different times, or with a different lookback window — this tool is how you check. Pair with resolution_diff to compare two markets directly. KNOWN GAP: idiosyncratic phrasing that doesn't match the vocabulary returns confidence:"low" and evidence_standard:"unspecified" rather than an LLM-guessed answer.

venue.description: Which venue to fetch the market from. "polymarket" is the offshore venue (polymarket.com); "polymarket-us" is the separate, CFTC-regulated polymarket.us venue, matched by slug via its own search (no exact-slug lookup exists upstream).

market.description: Polymarket (.com or .us) market slug or URL, OR a Kalshi market ticker (preferred) or event ticker (falls back to a representative market under that event).

definition.name: dailymed__resolution_diff_d593f2bf
definition.title: Resolution Diff
definition.description: Field-by-field diff of TWO markets' settlement clauses (one from each of `a` and `b`; either can be Polymarket .com, Polymarket US, or Kalshi) — runs resolution_audit on both sides and compares source, settle time, precision, comparison_basis, and evidence standard. Returns `equivalent`: "true" only when both sides parsed with enough confidence to compare AND no field conflicts; "false" when a specific conflict was found (differing_fields names which — e.g. ["source","settle_time"] for a Polymarket Bitcoin market settling on Binance's 1-minute candle at noon ET versus a Kalshi KXBTCD market settling on CF Benchmarks' BRTI 60-second average at 5pm EDT — SAME asset, DIFFERENT contract; or ["source","precision"] for Polymarket.com's Chainlink 15-minute TWAP clause (precision "twap_60s_lookback") against Kalshi's 15-minute KXBTC15M clause (precision "60-second trailing average" off CF Benchmarks' BRTI) — different source and a different lookback mechanism, even though BOTH compare an end-of-window average to a start-of-window average, so comparison_basis is EQUAL there and correctly NOT in differing_fields — verified live 2026-10-22, fleet #3447); "unclear" when one or both sides could not be confidently parsed (an absence of evidence is not evidence of equivalence — read raw_clause yourself in that case). comparison_basis is flagged as differing whenever both sides resolved one and they disagree, independent of whether source/precision also matched. Only flags source/evidence_standard as differing when BOTH sides gave a SPECIFIC comparable answer — a named source (e.g. "Associated Press, Fox News, NBC") against a generic one (e.g. Kalshi's "consensus of media organizations") is treated as the same evidence standard, not a conflict, since that is standard election-market boilerplate on both venues. Use this before sizing a polymarket_kalshi_spread pair as a real cross-venue arb, or standalone to sanity-check any two markets you suspect settle on different things.

definition.name: dailymed__release_calendar_markets_601a25ff
definition.title: Release Calendar Markets
definition.description: JOIN of the official release calendar (econ data, the FOMC, FDA decisions, SEC rules) against LIVE Polymarket/Kalshi markets — which scheduled releases land in the next N hours, and which live markets resolve on them. This is a POSITIONING tool, not a speed product: results are cached like every other pack (≤ 60s TTL) and there is no push/webhook — do not use this to try to beat a release, use it to see what is coming and what is already priced. CATEGORIES: econ (CPI, Employment Situation/jobs report, GDP, PCE, PPI, retail sales, housing starts, jobless claims — via fred_release_dates per known release_id, since FRED's own cross-release calendar mostly returns recent actuals, not future dates), fed (the next FOMC meeting's rate decision, via fomc_calendar), fda (PDUFA action dates + FDA advisory-committee meetings, via pdufa_catalysts / fda_adcom_calendar), sec (SEC final rules whose own DATES clause names an effective date in the window, via federal-register recent_rules — usually finds nothing in a short window since SEC rules typically take effect 30–60 days out, which is an accurate answer, not a bug), court (ALWAYS EMPTY today — court-listener has no forward-looking scheduled-hearing calendar, only filing/termination dates, so this category returns zero releases with unsupported:true rather than fabricate one). Omit `categories` or pass "all" for every category. MATCHING AND ITS HONESTY CONTRACT: every release is returned even when it has ZERO matched markets — a release is never dropped just because nothing on Polymarket or Kalshi resolves on it (most FDA/SEC releases will show markets:[]; that is signal, not a gap). Every matched market carries resolves_on_this_release: "true" (the venue's own close/end date sits within ~36h of the release AND the question passed a subject filter — econ and fed only), "likely" (same subject filter, but the venue closes days away from the release date), or "unclear" (a keyword hit with no date to anchor against — always true for the fda category, which has no ladder structure to check a date against). matched_by names the mechanism (a Kalshi series ticker, a Polymarket search query, or an FDA keyword probe) so a caller can judge the match rather than trust a label. scheduled_at carries both `utc` and `et`; econ releases use the standing BLS/Census 8:30am ET convention (FRED's calendar itself has no clock time), FOMC decisions use the 2:00pm ET convention, and FDA/SEC dates are date_only:true (no reliable clock time exists for either). DO NOT treat a matched market as a real arbitrage or a settled fact on its own — a market question sharing tokens with a release name is not proof it settles on that release's own published number. Call resolution_audit / resolution_diff (fleet #1909) on a specific market before sizing anything here. An empty window (zero releases across every requested category) returns the SAME shape as a populated one — release_count:0, releases:[] — plus empty_reason:"no_releases_in_window" and a `hint` telling you to widen, so you never branch on the response shape and never have to guess whether zero means "nothing is scheduled" or "the lookup failed". Econ releases especially cluster on specific dates each month, so a 48h window often straddles a dead stretch.

hours.description: Look-ahead window in hours from now. Default 48. Capped at 720 (30 days) — econ/fed releases are dated weeks apart, so a short window is often empty; widen rather than assume nothing is scheduled.

categories.description: Comma or space separated subset of econ|fed|fda|sec|court, or "all" (default). E.g. "econ,fed" or "fda".

empty_reason.description: Present ONLY on a zero-release window: "no_releases_in_window". The window was queried and nothing is scheduled — this is an answer, not a failure.

hint.description: Present ONLY on a zero-release window: what to change (usually a wider `hours`).

definition.name: dailymed__prediction_calibration_99b4283c
definition.title: Prediction Calibration
definition.description: REALIZED win rate by shown price and minutes elapsed for short-horizon crypto up/down markets, net of taker fee — read from our own settled-outcomes archive, not from live prices. Answers the one question no venue will: "a side shown at 82 with five minutes left, how often did it ACTUALLY win?" Returns a grid of (price bucket x minute elapsed) -> n, realized_win_rate_pp, mean_shown_price_pp, calibration_gap_pp (realized minus shown — zero means the book is calibrated), breakeven_win_rate_pp (the shown price plus the taker fee that was actually in force for that market), and net_edge_pp (realized minus breakeven, which is what a taker would have kept). WHY AN ARCHIVE EXISTS AT ALL: a settled 15-minute window is exactly what these venues stop serving. Measured 2026-10-22, a polymarket.com window drops out of the default market listing within minutes of closing (its trade tape and resolution stay retrievable by a closed-market lookup, which the collector now uses), and the other venues serve settled windows only briefly or thinly. So this tool reads a local archive collected window-by-window as they settle. THE THREE VENUES ARE NEVER POOLED. all three compare an END 60-second average with a START 60-second average, but on different feeds: polymarket.com on a Chainlink TWAP, polymarket-us and Kalshi on a CF Benchmarks BRTI simple average. The feeds disagree near the threshold (measured 2026-10-24 on btc: polymarket.com and Kalshi settled differently on 1.6% of windows both hold, polymarket-us and Kalshi on none), so venue:"all" returns one grid PER VENUE and `venues_pooled` is always false. EVERY RATE CARRIES ITS 95% INTERVAL, AND EVERY EDGE SAYS WHETHER IT SURVIVES IT. Each cell gives realized_win_rate_ci95_lo/hi_pp (Wilson, so it never reports an impossible win rate above 100), the same interval carried onto net_edge_ci95_lo/hi_pp, and net_edge_distinguishable_from_zero. READ THAT BOOLEAN BEFORE net_edge_pp: at these sample sizes most cells are false, meaning the interval straddles zero and a net_edge_pp of +4pp is NOT evidence of an edge. For scale, at a 90% win rate even n=300 gives a 95% half-width of ~3.4pp while net edges here run +2 to +4pp — so a comfortable-looking sample still cannot call a small edge real. `verdict` says it per cell in plain words, and the first note says how many cells survived. A THIN CELL WITHHOLDS ITS RATE ENTIRELY. Any bucket holding fewer than 30 settled windows reports status "thin" with realized_win_rate_pp and every interval null rather than printing a rate from a sample too small to mean anything — a 2-sample "100% win rate" is the most misleading thing this tool could say. ALWAYS READ `coverage` BEFORE THE GRID: it gives the first and last window held, windows_total vs windows_settled, every UTC day inside the span with no windows at all, and the longest run of consecutive missing windows. A grid over a store with a three-day hole looks entirely normal and is measuring a different population. mean_fill_price_pp and fill_vs_shown_pp are populated for polymarket.com only — it is the one venue of the three that publishes a trade tape for these markets, so it is the only place realized FILL can be compared with the shown price instead of assumed equal to it.

venue.description: polymarket | polymarket-us | kalshi | all (default polymarket). "all" returns one grid per venue, never a merged one.

asset.description: btc (default) | eth | sol | xrp | bnb. Coverage differs by venue: polymarket and polymarket-us carry btc/eth/sol/xrp, Kalshi carries btc/eth/bnb.

horizon.description: 15m (default). 5m | 1h | 1d are accepted but only 15m is collected today, so another value returns coverage.windows_total 0 rather than an error.

bucket_pp.description: Price-bucket width in percentage points: 5 | 10 (default) | 20 | 25 | 50. Must divide 100, so the last bucket is never narrower than the rest.

minute.description: Minutes elapsed since window open, 0-based. Omit for the full grid; pass 5 for the "five minutes in" row only, which is also the cheapest query.

side_convention.description: "favorite" (default) folds each window onto whichever side was the favorite — the frame published claims about early favorites use. "yes" keeps the venue own YES/Up side.

definition.name: dailymed__updown_venue_compare_2bbd74e7
definition.title: Updown Venue Compare
definition.description: The same 15-minute crypto "up or down" window priced on polymarket.com, Polymarket US and Kalshi, side by side, with whether each pair is actually the same contract. Pass asset (btc | eth | sol | xrp | bnb) and window ("current" default, "next", "previous", or the window START as ISO such as 2026-10-27T14:15:00Z, on a 15-minute boundary). Per venue: question, Up bid / ask / mid / last, spread_pp, quote_state, volume WITH ITS UNIT, open interest, liquidity, settlement source, comparison basis, when it settles. THE VENUES ARE NOT ONE CONTRACT. Kalshi and Polymarket US settle on CF Benchmarks' BRTI (60-second average at the end against the same at the start): the same bet, so a gap between them is a real disagreement. polymarket.com settles on a Chainlink 60-second TWAP, end against start: same comparison shape, different feed, so a gap against either is partly the contract. `pairs[]` gives equivalent ("true"|"false"|"unclear"|"not_comparable") from resolution_diff for every pair, material_differences, mid_diff_pp (a minus b, in percentage points) and read_as in words. Measured over 30 days of settled windows the Chainlink and BRTI feeds settle a window differently about 1.2-1.8% of the time, almost entirely windows that ended near the threshold (see updown_divergence_rate). `net_spread` is computed only for the pair that is equivalent: the gap in mid terms and at top of book (buy Up where cheaper at the ask, Down where Up is dearer at 1 minus the bid) after BOTH venues' taker fees, each fee carrying its verified-as-of date. Top-of-book size is shown where the venue publishes it (Polymarket US); the Kalshi figure is not in its market payload, so read its order book before sizing. A venue with no market for the window is {status:"not_listed", reason}; one that could not be read is {status:"unavailable", refusal} -- never an empty object, and never the same thing. A one-sided book (typical Polymarket US just before a window is decided) has quote_state "bid_only", a null mid, and the last trade stands in labelled price_basis "last". Quotes are read venue by venue (cached up to 60 seconds), so a gap of a couple of points on a moving window is inside the skew. Only the 15m horizon is offered: it is the one where all three list the same up/down question. For the settled history of how often the venues disagreed, call updown_divergence_rate.

asset.description: btc (default) | eth | sol | xrp | bnb. Coverage differs by venue; a venue that does not list the asset answers not_listed.

window.description: "current" (default), "next", "previous", or the window START as an ISO-8601 timestamp on a 15-minute boundary, e.g. 2026-10-27T14:15:00Z. An unaligned timestamp is refused, not rounded.

definition.name: dailymed__updown_divergence_rate_f4699a7c
definition.title: Updown Divergence Rate
definition.description: How often two venues settled the SAME 15-minute crypto window differently, over every settled window on record. Compares polymarket.com (Chainlink TWAP) with Kalshi and with Polymarket US (both CF Benchmarks BRTI), and Kalshi with Polymarket US as the same-feed control. Per pair: windows both venues settled, divergent count, the rate with its 95% Wilson interval (withheld under 30 paired windows), which direction they split, and what was excluded (unsettled on a side, 50-50). A HEADLINE RATE IS A CONCENTRATION QUESTION, so every pair also carries `concentration` (UTC days and hours the divergent windows fell in, the busiest day, the top-3-day share, and a plain reading) and `by_how_decided` (the rate by how far the reference venue's mid was from 50 at its last priced minute: the rate is a fraction of a percent for windows that were decided by the end and tens of percent for the ones that were not). `divergent_path` gives the mean Up mid by minute on both venues over the divergent windows only, split by who said Up, so the "early spike that fades" story can be checked rather than assumed. Measured on the archive 2026-10-27 over 30 days of btc: polymarket.com vs Kalshi diverged on 48 of 2,847 windows (1.69%, interval 1.27-2.23), spread over 27 of 31 UTC days, 0.19% of windows decided by the end and 17-29% of the ones still undecided; Polymarket US vs Kalshi on 0 of 1,838. asset btc | eth | sol | xrp | bnb (bnb has no pair: Kalshi only); days 1-90 (default 30), capped by what the archive holds (it starts 2026-09-22 for polymarket.com and Kalshi, 2026-10-07 for Polymarket US). Read-only; cheap enough to call, it reads several thousand archive rows.

asset.description: btc (default) | eth | sol | xrp | bnb. The archive holds btc/eth on all three venues, sol/xrp on polymarket.com and Polymarket US, bnb on Kalshi only (no pair).

days.description: Look-back in days, 1-90 (default 30). The archive starts 2026-09-22 (polymarket.com, Kalshi) and 2026-10-07 (Polymarket US, btc), so a longer span is capped by what is held; coverage is reported per pair.

definition.name: dailymed__archive_evidence_8a1688de
definition.title: Archive Evidence
definition.description: What did a web page say on a given date? Finds the archived capture of a URL nearest that date across the Internet Archive Wayback Machine, Common Crawl and Arquivo.pt, reads it, and returns the readable text (HTML stripped) with the capture timestamp, a link to the archived copy, and the GAP between the date asked for and the capture actually used (e.g. "Captured 1.5 day(s) before the requested date"). One call replaces the find-capture, fetch-record, parse-HTML chain. If no archive holds a capture within max_gap_days (default 30) it answers status "no_capture" and names the nearest capture before and after the date with their gaps, so a distant capture is never passed off as the page on that date. Every archive's outcome is listed in sources[]; one that timed out or errored says so with its upstream status, and if all of them failed the answer is error "archives_unavailable", not no_capture. Captures are immutable and cached by capture id; served_from says whether the text came from cache or upstream. Use archive_compare to see what changed between two dates.

date.description: The date to look up, as YYYY-MM-DD (e.g. "2023-06-01"), YYYYMMDD, or a full ISO timestamp.

max_gap_days.description: Furthest a capture may be from the date and still be used, in days. Default 30, max 3650.

max_chars.description: Characters of page text to return. Default 12000, max 60000.

definition.name: dailymed__archive_compare_1ab17622
definition.title: Archive Compare
definition.description: What changed on a web page between two dates? Resolves the archived capture nearest each date (Internet Archive Wayback Machine, Common Crawl, Arquivo.pt), extracts the readable text of both, and returns a text-level diff: the segments removed and added, a similarity score, and both capture timestamps with their gaps from the requested dates. It diffs readable text, not markup, so a restyled page with the same words reads changed:false. Identical captures answer changed:false with the reason (same capture, identical content digest, or identical text), never an empty diff. A date with no capture within max_gap_days (default 30) answers status "no_capture", naming which side is missing and the nearest captures to it. Typical uses: how a privacy policy, terms of service, pricing or product page changed; whether a statement was on a page at a given time.

max_gap_days.description: Furthest a capture may be from each date and still be used, in days. Default 30, max 3650.

definition.name: dailymed__research_row_c01b2a4f
definition.title: Research Row
definition.description: Claygent-style per-row research: answer ONE question about ONE company and return a JSON object matching your output_schema, with every field wrapped in its own evidence — {value, evidence_url, quote, status}. status is NEVER self-reported by the model: "found" means this code independently verified the model's quote is a VERBATIM substring of text actually fetched; "inferred" means a value was given but the quote could not be verified; "not_established" means no source answered the field, and its value is always null — never guessed, never a blended score. Sources: "web" fetches the company's own site (entity.domain required — homepage, /about, /leadership) via fetch_url; "catalog" checks entity_profile (SEC EDGAR; resolved:false for a private company is expected, not a failure); "both" (default) tries both. max_cost (USD, default 0.02, max 0.50) scales how many pages are fetched and refuses up front if it is too small to pay for even one extraction call (floor $0.002) — never silently overspends. A row where every source comes back empty costs nothing: every field is mechanically not_established with NO model call made. For a boolean/derived field (e.g. "does this company sell to healthcare"), the quote only has to SUPPORT the value — a descriptive sentence about customers/products counts, the source need not state the answer verbatim. leadership_page_status ("fetched"|"not_found"|"not_attempted", plus leadership_note) says plainly whether a leadership/team page was actually read, so a named-person field (head_of_sales) coming back not_established is distinguishable from "this company just doesn't publish one" vs. "we never checked". model_output_empty:true means the model returned nothing usable (a transport/budget problem) — every field is not_established for THAT reason, never read as 20 individual "no" judgments. Use with a fixed question + schema across many rows for "Claygent over N companies with a hard cost cap" (composes with batch callers). For picking from a fixed label list instead of extracting open fields, use classify_row (cheaper, one model call).

entity.description: The row/company to research. At least one of name/domain required.

domain.description: Company website domain, e.g. "acme.com" (with or without https://). Required to use sources:"web".

question.description: The question to answer about this company, in natural language, e.g. "Does this company sell to healthcare, and who is the head of sales?"

output_schema.description: JSON Schema object naming the fields to extract, e.g. {"properties":{"sells_to_healthcare":{"type":"boolean"},"head_of_sales":{"type":"string"}}}. Up to 20 fields.

sources.description: Where to look: "web" (company site only), "catalog" (entity_profile only), "both" (default).

max_cost.description: Cost ceiling in US dollars for this one row. Default 0.02, max 0.50, minimum viable 0.002 (below that the call is refused rather than silently exceeding it).

examples.question: Does this company sell to healthcare, and who is the head of sales?

definition.name: dailymed__classify_row_0724896a
definition.title: Classify Row
definition.description: Cheap categorization: given a company and a list of candidate labels, decide which labels apply — the most common GTM/AI usage shape (tagging a list by industry, ICP fit, etc.), one small model call. Same evidence contract as research_row: each label comes back {label, applies, evidence_url, quote, status: found|inferred|not_established} — "found" only when the model's quote is independently verified as a verbatim substring of the text used. Pass text directly (cheapest — no fetch) or entity.domain to fetch the homepage once as a fallback. No text and no domain means every label is not_established with no model call made.

entity.description: The row/company to classify. At least one of name/domain required.

domain.description: Company website domain — used to fetch the homepage ONLY when text is not provided.

labels.description: Candidate labels to test, 2-30 strings, e.g. ["healthcare","fintech","logistics"].

text.description: Text to classify directly (a description, a page you already fetched, etc.) — cheapest path, skips any fetch.

definition.name: dailymed__pipeworx_trending_2763df58
definition.title: Pipeworx Trending
definition.description: What other AI agents are calling on Pipeworx right now. Returns the top tools, top packs, and total call volume over a recent window (24h, 7d, or 30d). Useful for: (1) discovering what data sources are hot for current events, (2) confirming a popular tool is the canonical choice before asking your own question, (3) seeing whether your use case aligns with what most agents need. Self-aggregating signal — derived from CF analytics-engine, no PII, just (pack, tool, count). Cached 5min-1h depending on window.

window.description: 24h (default) | 7d | 30d. Shorter windows surface what's hot right now; longer windows show steady-state demand.

definition.name: dailymed__suggest_questions_39f8d439
definition.title: What Can I Ask Pipeworx?
definition.description: What can I ask Pipeworx? / what is Pipeworx good for? / what can you do? / give me ideas / show me examples / getting started / what data do you have? — the onboarding entry point for an agent that just connected and wants to know what is worth asking. Returns category-bucketed example questions (company financials, drugs & clinical trials, economics, real estate, prediction markets, weather, government & patents, science & academia, news) — each with the exact tool + argument shape that answers it, drawn from the live catalog of thousands of tools. Call with no arguments for the full spread, or pass `topic` (e.g. "finance", "pharma", "betting") to focus. Use this FIRST when you do not yet know what Pipeworx can do for you, or to learn how to call the meta-tools (ask_pipeworx, entity_profile, compare_entities, etc.).

topic.description: Optional focus area: finance | pharma | economics | real-estate | betting | weather | government | science | news. Omit for a cross-category spread.

definition.name: dailymed__generate_llms_txt_192805b5
definition.title: Generate llms.txt
definition.description: Generate a production-ready llms.txt file for any URL so AI crawlers (ChatGPT, Claude, Perplexity) can index the site cleanly. Fetches the page, extracts title/description/key links, and emits the standard llms.txt markdown format. Output is a single text blob ready to drop at site-root/llms.txt. Useful for: getting a client's site indexed by AI, drafting llms.txt for your own project, or auditing how an AI crawler would see a competitor.

url.description: Full URL of the site to summarize, e.g. "https://example.com" or a specific landing page.

max_links.description: Maximum number of link entries to include (default 25, max 50).

definition.name: dailymed__ai_visibility_check_2332d098
definition.title: AI Visibility Check
definition.description: Probe one or more LLMs for what they know about a business / brand / product / topic and score visibility (0-100) per model. Default model is Workers AI Llama-3.3-70b (free); pass `_apiKey` to also probe Anthropic (BYO key — you pay Anthropic directly for those calls). Returns per-model {score, confidence, signals, raw_response} + a combined view. Useful for AI-marketing audits, pre-launch brand checks, competitive monitoring.

entity.description: The thing to ask about. Brand/business name, product name, person, or topic. E.g. "Pipeworx", "OpenInvoice", "Acme Corp pricing".

context.description: Optional: a phrase locating the entity (e.g. "Boston restaurant", "B2B SaaS"). Helps disambiguate common names.

models.description: Which models to probe. Supported: "workers-ai" (free default), "anthropic" (requires _apiKey). Omit for just workers-ai.

_apiKey.description: Optional Anthropic API key (sk-ant-...) — only needed if "anthropic" is in models. Passed straight through to api.anthropic.com.

definition.name: dailymed__scan_competitor_ai_presence_682a351f
definition.title: Scan Competitor AI Presence
definition.description: Compare AI visibility across multiple entities side-by-side. Probes each entity (your brand + N competitors) with ai_visibility_check, ranks by score, surfaces which is most/least recognized. Useful for competitive AI-marketing audits: "does Claude know about us as well as our competitors?". Returns ranked list with score, confidence, signal density per entity.

entities.description: Array of 2-8 entities to compare (brand/business/product names). First entry treated as the "subject" for narrative; rest are competitors.

context.description: Optional shared context applied to every probe (e.g. "B2B SaaS", "Boston restaurant"). Disambiguates common names.

models.description: Which models to probe. Supported: "workers-ai" (free default), "anthropic" (requires _apiKey). Omit for just workers-ai.

_apiKey.description: Optional Anthropic API key — only if "anthropic" is in models. Passed to api.anthropic.com per probe.

definition.name: dailymed__pipeworx_feedback_5bb126f6
definition.title: Send Pipeworx Feedback
definition.description: Tell the Pipeworx team something is broken, missing, or needs to exist. Use when a tool returns wrong/stale data (bug), when a tool you wish existed isn't in the catalog (feature/data_gap), or when something worked surprisingly well (praise). ONLY for tools served by this Pipeworx connection — if the tool came from a different MCP server in your client (another vendor's Gmail, Splunk, Slack, etc. connector), we cannot fix it and reporting it here only delays you; file it with that server instead. Not sure? Pipeworx tool names are the ones this connection lists. Describe the issue in terms of Pipeworx tools/packs — don't paste the end-user's prompt. Filing without an account returns a `claim_token`; pass it back later as pipeworx_feedback({claim_token:"pwfb_…"}) to read whether it was fixed and what changed. The team reads digests daily and signal directly affects roadmap. Rate-limited to 5 per identifier per day. Free; doesn't count against your tool-call quota.

type.description: bug = something broke or returned wrong data. feature = a new tool or capability you wish existed. data_gap = data Pipeworx does not currently expose. praise = positive note. other = anything else.

message.description: Your feedback in plain text. Be specific (which tool, what error, what data was missing). 1-2 sentences typical, 2000 chars max.

context.description: Optional structured context: which tool, pack, or vertical this relates to.

claim_token.description: Read the reply to a report you filed earlier: pass the `pwfb_…` token that filing returned, with no other arguments. Returns the status and, once resolved, what actually changed.

examples.message: Fleet #2184 smoke test: verifying pipeworx_feedback example call returns non-empty.

definition.name: dailymed__remember_c772528d
definition.title: Remember
definition.description: Save data the agent will need to reuse later — across this conversation or across sessions. Use when you discover something worth carrying forward (a resolved ticker, a target address, a user preference, a research subject) so you don't have to look it up again. Stored as a key-value pair scoped by your identifier. Authenticated users get persistent memory; anonymous sessions retain memory for 24 hours. Pair with recall to retrieve later, forget to delete.

key.description: Memory key (e.g., "subject_property", "target_ticker", "user_preference"). Accepts name, k, label as aliases.

value.description: Value to store (any text — findings, addresses, preferences, notes). Accepts content, text, data, v as aliases; a non-string value is stored as JSON.

definition.name: dailymed__recall_a4265905
definition.title: Recall
definition.description: Retrieve a value previously saved via remember, or list all saved keys (omit the key argument). Use to look up context the agent stored earlier — the user's target ticker, an address, prior research notes — without re-deriving it from scratch. Scoped to your identifier (anonymous IP, BYO key hash, or account ID). Pair with remember to save, forget to delete.

key.description: Memory key to retrieve (omit to list all keys). Accepts name, k, label as aliases.

definition.name: dailymed__forget_204eaab0
definition.title: Forget
definition.description: Delete a previously stored memory by key. Use when context is stale, the task is done, or you want to clear sensitive data the agent saved earlier. Pair with remember and recall.

key.description: Memory key to delete. Accepts name, k, label as aliases.

definition.name: dailymed__search_drugs_f13416c9
definition.title: Search Drugs
definition.description: Search Structured Product Labels by any combination of name, ANDA/NDA, NDC, RxCUI.

outputSchema.description: Search results for Structured Product Labels

definition.name: dailymed__get_drug_7f7ff508
definition.title: Get Drug
definition.description: FULL FDA DRUG LABEL TEXT from the current DailyMed Structured Product Label — indications, dosage and administration, contraindications, warnings and precautions, boxed warning, adverse reactions, and every other labeled section, as readable plain text. Pass a DRUG NAME ("Ozempic", "ibuprofen") and it resolves the label automatically, or a DailyMed set_id. PREFER OVER WEB SEARCH for "what are the warnings for X", "what is X indicated for", "what is the dose of X", "does X have a boxed warning". Returns the label title, labeler, SPL version and publication date alongside the sections.

drug_name.description: Drug brand or generic name (e.g. "Ozempic", "ibuprofen"). Resolved to the primary manufacturer's label. Use this OR set_id.

set_id.description: DailyMed SET ID UUID, when you already have one. Takes precedence over drug_name.

section.description: Optional case-insensitive substring filter, matched against both the section heading and its LOINC category, e.g. "boxed warning", "warnings", "dosage", "indications". Omit for the whole label.

max_section_chars.description: Truncate each section body to this many characters (default 4000, max 40000).

sections.description: SPL sections (dosage, warnings, adverse reactions, etc.)

content.description: Section content HTML or plain text

outputSchema.description: Full Structured Product Label with metadata and sections

definition.name: dailymed__list_labels_for_drug_name_e11effd1
definition.title: List Labels For Drug Name
definition.description: All labels mentioning a drug name.

definition.name: dailymed__recent_updates_0899f7fc
definition.title: Recent Updates
definition.description: Return the most recently updated FDA Structured Product Labels from DailyMed (NLM), up to 100 results, ordered by update date descending. Useful for tracking newly revised drug labeling.

limit.description: 1-100 (default 25)

definition.name: dailymed__label_history_b0d4ac92
definition.title: Label History
definition.description: Drug LABEL REVISION HISTORY — when a prescription drug's FDA label was revised, and how many times. Pass a DRUG NAME ("Ozempic", "semaglutide") and it resolves to that drug's Structured Product Label automatically; or pass a DailyMed set_id directly. PREFER OVER WEB SEARCH for "has the label for X changed recently", "when was X's label last updated", "how many label revisions does X have", label-change monitoring, and safety-labeling-change surveillance. Returns every published SPL version with its date, plus official archive URLs where DailyMed exposes them. Use before label_diff to see which versions are downloadable and pick two to compare.

drug_name.description: Drug brand or generic name (e.g. "Ozempic", "semaglutide"). Resolved to the primary manufacturer's label (the most-revised SPL for that name, over repackager duplicates). Use this OR set_id.

set_id.description: DailyMed SET ID UUID, when you already have one. Takes precedence over drug_name.

definition.name: dailymed__label_diff_7340d4fc
definition.title: Label Diff
definition.description: WHAT CHANGED between two versions of a drug's FDA label — conservative section-level text comparison of official DailyMed SPL versions. Pass a DRUG NAME ("Ozempic") and it resolves the label automatically; or pass a set_id. Defaults to the latest version versus its immediate predecessor. PREFER OVER WEB SEARCH for "what changed in X's label", "new warnings added to X", "did X get a boxed warning", label-change diffing. Reports added, removed, and changed sections with normalized before/after text. Reports textual change only and leaves clinical materiality to the caller.

drug_name.description: Drug brand or generic name (e.g. "Ozempic"). Resolved to the primary manufacturer's label. Use this OR set_id.

set_id.description: DailyMed SET ID UUID, when you already have one. Takes precedence over drug_name.

from_version.description: Older SPL version. Defaults to the version immediately before the latest.

to_version.description: Newer SPL version. Defaults to the latest version.

max_sections.description: Maximum section records returned (1-100, default 25); counts cover all sections.

definition.name: dailymed__list_classes_411d11c4
definition.title: List Classes
definition.description: List pharmacologic drug-class reference entries from DailyMed, optionally filtered by class_code or class type (EPC = established pharmacologic class, MoA = mechanism of action, PE = physiologic effect, CS = chemical structure). Returns class codes and display names. ~1,210 classes total, 100 per page.

class_code.description: Restrict to a specific class code. NLM RxClass format, e.g. "N0000175809" — not a UMLS CUI.

type.description: EPC | MoA | PE | CS

page.description: 1-based page (100 per page, ~13 pages). Ignored when class_code is given.

definition.name: crossref__crossref_get_work_06094c12
definition.title: Get Work by DOI
definition.description: Resolves a DOI to its full Crossref metadata record: title, authors, editors, affiliations, abstract (when deposited), journal or container with the volume, issue, pages, and article number that locate the work in it, ISSNs and ISBNs, publication date, type, license, full-text links, and funder acknowledgements. The author list is paged: authorCount is the full deposited total, offset and limit select the page (25 authors by default), and when authors remain the response carries a nextOffset to pass back as offset — large-collaboration papers deposit thousands. Post-publication updates are relayed as Crossref records them: updatedBy names each correction, retraction, expression of concern, or new version issued against this work, with its notice DOI and whether the publisher or Retraction Watch recorded it, and updateTo names the works this record is itself a notice for. An absent updatedBy does not mean the work was never updated — coverage depends on those deposits. relations lists related identifiers, such as a preprint and its published version, grouped by relation type; only the Crossref-registered DOIs among them resolve through crossref_get_work. memberId is the Crossref member that holds the DOI now — pass it to crossref_get_member for the publisher record and its deposit coverage; the prefix of the DOI names the member that registered the prefix, which for a transferred title is a former publisher. Outgoing references are reported as a count in referencesCount; the reference entries themselves come from crossref_get_references. The isReferencedByCount field reports the total incoming citation count from Crossref; the citing works themselves are not available through Crossref — use OpenAlex for citation graphs.

doi.description: DOI in the format "10.NNNN/suffix", e.g. "10.1038/nature12373". A resolver-wrapped form — "https://doi.org/10.1038/nature12373", "https://dx.doi.org/…", "doi:10.1038/nature12373" — is accepted and unwrapped.

offset.description: Zero-based index of the first author to return. Pass the nextOffset value from the previous response to continue through a long author list. Only the author list is paged; every other field of the record is returned in full on every page.

limit.description: Maximum number of authors to return in one page (1–10000 per call, default 25). A larger value, up to 100000, returns 10000 and says so in notice; nextOffset continues after the authors returned. Ordinary records fit in a single page; large-collaboration papers in particle physics and genomics deposit thousands.

doi.description: Canonical DOI

type.description: Work type (e.g. journal-article, book-chapter, posted-content)

authors.description: Page of the author and contributor list, bounded by limit. Omitted when the record deposits no author field at all.

name.description: Name when no given/family split is available
Affiliation name as deposited. Absent when the publisher asserted the organization by identifier alone, where ror carries it instead.

ror.description: ROR identifier for the affiliated organization, when the deposit carries one. It is the whole identity of an affiliation deposited without a name.

items.description: Affiliation
Author or contributor

authorCount.description: Total number of authors in the deposited list, before offset and limit were applied. Omitted alongside authors when the record deposits no author field.

offset.description: Zero-based index of the first returned author within the deposited list. Omitted alongside authors when the record deposits no author field.

editors.description: Editors of the work, or of the book or proceedings containing it, in the entry shape authors use. Returned whole — never paged by offset and limit, and never counted in authorCount. Omitted when the record deposits none.

name.description: Name when no given/family split is available
Affiliation name as deposited. Absent when the publisher asserted the organization by identifier alone, where ror carries it instead.

ror.description: ROR identifier for the affiliated organization, when the deposit carries one. It is the whole identity of an affiliation deposited without a name.

items.description: Affiliation
Author or contributor

updatedBy.description: Update notices Crossref records against this work — corrections, errata, retractions, expressions of concern, withdrawals, new versions — in deposited order. Entries are never merged: the same notice DOI can appear once per source, typed differently by each. Omitted when none is recorded, which does not mean the work was never updated: coverage depends on publisher and Retraction Watch deposits.

doi.description: DOI on the other side of the link: the notice, in updatedBy; the updated work, in updateTo. It is this work's own DOI when the update was made to this record in place.

type.description: Crossref update type as deposited: correction, erratum, corrigendum, addendum, retraction, withdrawal, expression_of_concern, new_version, new_edition, or another code

source.description: Who recorded the link: publisher, or retraction-watch for an entry Crossref carries from the Retraction Watch database

recordId.description: Retraction Watch record ID. Present only on retraction-watch entries.

items.description: Update link

updateTo.description: Works this record is an update notice for, in the entry shape updatedBy uses and in deposited order. Omitted when the record is not registered as a notice.

doi.description: DOI on the other side of the link: the notice, in updatedBy; the updated work, in updateTo. It is this work's own DOI when the update was made to this record in place.

type.description: Crossref update type as deposited: correction, erratum, corrigendum, addendum, retraction, withdrawal, expression_of_concern, new_version, new_edition, or another code

source.description: Who recorded the link: publisher, or retraction-watch for an entry Crossref carries from the Retraction Watch database

recordId.description: Retraction Watch record ID. Present only on retraction-watch entries.

definition.name: crossref__crossref_get_references_9b005784
definition.title: Get Reference List
definition.description: Returns the outgoing reference list for a DOI — the works cited by this paper. Each reference includes the deposited citation string and, where Crossref has resolved it, a DOI you can look up with crossref_get_work. Results are paged: referenceCount is the full deposited total, and when more remain the response carries a nextOffset to pass back as offset. Reference list coverage varies by publisher; many older works and non-participating publishers have no indexed references. Incoming citations — the works that cite this paper — are not available through Crossref; use OpenAlex for that.

doi.description: DOI in the format "10.NNNN/suffix", e.g. "10.1038/nature12373". A resolver-wrapped form — "https://doi.org/10.1038/nature12373", "https://dx.doi.org/…", "doi:10.1038/nature12373" — is accepted and unwrapped.

limit.description: Maximum number of references to return in one page (1–2500 per call, default 100). A larger value, up to 100000, returns 2500 and says so in notice; nextOffset continues after the references returned. Most works fit in a single page; bibliography records can carry tens of thousands.

referenceCount.description: Total number of references in the deposited list

definition.name: crossref__crossref_search_works_8a0ff4d0
definition.title: Search Works
definition.description: Searches the Crossref works index (~188M records) by free text and/or structured filters. The generic query matches loosely across all fields; scope precisely with the field-specific parameters queryTitle, queryAuthor, and queryContainerTitle, or resolve a known citation to its DOI with queryBibliographic — all combine with each other and with query. Use the filter parameter for structured filtering (object with hyphen-separated Crossref keys). Sort options: relevance, score, is-referenced-by-count, published, deposited, indexed, created. Each work returns at most authorLimit authors (25 by default) with authorCount reporting the full deposited total, since a single page of large-collaboration papers can carry tens of thousands of author entries; crossref_get_work pages the whole author list for any DOI whose list was cut. Post-publication updates ride each work as Crossref records them: updatedBy names each correction, retraction, expression of concern, or new version issued against it, and updateTo the works it is itself a notice for — an absent updatedBy does not mean the work was never updated. Offset-based paging is capped at ~10K results; use cursor="*" to start cursor-based deep paging, then pass the nextCursor value from each response to continue. A walk with a query term and no sort runs by relevance, one with filters only in Crossref registration order. The walk ends on the page where nextCursor is absent — that page also carries a notice saying the list is exhausted. Cursor and offset cannot be combined.

query.description: Free-text search query, e.g. "CRISPR gene editing" or "climate change adaptation"

queryBibliographic.description: Whole-citation match to resolve a known reference to its DOI. Combine title, author, year, and container into one string, e.g. "Watson Crick molecular structure of nucleic acids Nature 1953".

queryTitle.description: Match against work titles only, e.g. "Array programming with NumPy".

queryAuthor.description: Match against author names only, e.g. "Charles R. Harris".

queryContainerTitle.description: Match against the container title (journal or book name) only, e.g. "Nature".

filter.description: Structured filter object using Crossref hyphen-separated keys. All values must be strings. Boolean flag keys (has-abstract, has-references, has-full-text) require string values "true" or "false". Example: {"type":"journal-article","has-abstract":"true","from-pub-date":"2023-01-01"}

fields.description: Fields to return (reduces payload). Names are case-sensitive, and each fills one output field: DOI → doi, title → title, type → type, author → authors and authorCount, published / published-print / published-online → published, container-title → containerTitle and containerTitles, publisher → publisher, member → memberId, is-referenced-by-count → isReferencedByCount, score → score, abstract → abstract, volume → volume, issue → issue, page → page, article-number → articleNumber, ISSN → issn, updated-by → updatedBy, update-to → updateTo. A selected field absent from a work means the record does not deposit it. DOI is always returned whether or not it is listed here, so every result stays resolvable by crossref_get_work, which also returns the fields this list does not cover (license, funder, references, and the rest of the record).

items.description: Crossref select name

rows.description: Number of results to return per page (1–250 per call, default 20). A larger value, up to 1000, returns 250 and says so in notice — on an offset page the notice also names the offset that continues after the records returned.

authorLimit.description: Maximum number of authors to return per work (1–500 per call, default 25; a larger value, up to 100000, applies 500 and says so in notice). Ordinary records fit under the default; large-collaboration papers deposit thousands, and a page of them is large enough to exhaust a client context. Each work reports its full deposited total as authorCount — call crossref_get_work with that work doi to page the authors this cap left out.

offset.description: Zero-based result offset for offset-based paging. Cannot be used with cursor. Capped at ~10K: offset + rows cannot pass it, so a page that would returns the rows that fit and says so in notice, and an offset at or past it is refused. Use cursor for deeper paging.

cursor.description: Cursor token for deep paging. Pass "*" to start cursor-based paging (required past ~10K results), then pass the nextCursor value from each response until a response omits it, which means the list is exhausted. A walk with a query term runs by relevance unless sort is set; a walk with filters only runs in Crossref registration order. Relevance scores shift slightly between identical requests, so a relevance walk can repeat or skip a record at a page boundary — sort:"created" walks every match without repeats. Cannot be combined with offset, or with a publication-date sort (published, published-print, published-online), which Crossref does not walk by cursor.

sort.description: Sort field. Omitted, an offset page with a query term is ranked by relevance, and so is a cursor walk with one (sent as score). The publication-date sorts (published, published-print, published-online) work with offset paging only — Crossref refuses them alongside cursor; every other sort works with either.

order.description: Sort direction (asc or desc). Applies only alongside sort; without one it has no effect.

doi.description: Canonical DOI

type.description: Work type

authors.description: Author list for this work, capped at authorLimit. Omitted when the record deposits no author field.

name.description: Name when no given/family split is available

items.description: Author

authorCount.description: Total number of authors deposited for this work, before the authorLimit cap. Greater than the length of authors when the cap cut the list; pass the doi of this work to crossref_get_work to page the whole list.

published.description: Publication date — the first of published, published-print, and published-online that names one. A component Crossref records as unknown is omitted, and so is every component below it.

containerTitle.description: Journal or container name — the first entry of containerTitles

containerTitles.description: Every container title the record deposits, in deposited order. A book chapter or proceedings paper often deposits two: the series, then the book or volume. Omitted when the record deposits none.

volume.description: Volume of the container the work appears in

issue.description: Issue of the container the work appears in

articleNumber.description: Article number, deposited by journals that number articles instead of paging them

memberId.description: Crossref member ID of the publisher that holds this DOI now — pass to crossref_get_member for its record. The DOI's prefix names the member that registered the prefix, which for a transferred title is a former publisher. Omitted when the record deposits no member.

updatedBy.description: Update notices Crossref records against this work — corrections, errata, retractions, expressions of concern, withdrawals, new versions — in deposited order. Entries are never merged: the same notice DOI can appear once per source, typed differently by each. Omitted when none is recorded, which does not mean the work was never updated: coverage depends on publisher and Retraction Watch deposits.

updateTo.description: Works this record is an update notice for, in the entry shape updatedBy uses and in deposited order. Omitted when the record is not registered as a notice.

type.description: Crossref update type as deposited: correction, erratum, corrigendum, addendum, retraction, withdrawal, expression_of_concern, new_version, new_edition, or another code

recordId.description: Retraction Watch record ID. Present only on retraction-watch entries.

abstract.description: Abstract when present in the indexed record — the text of the publisher’s JATS deposit, with markup removed and character references decoded; numeric JATS superscripts retain caret notation (10^{16}, GeV^2), a link keeps its tag only where its href holds an address the text it wraps does not already carry, and each formula appears once — MathML as the TeX annotation it carries, otherwise written out linearly (x_i, A^{−1}, √(m), (a+b)/c), and TeX deposited beside MathML in whichever notation comes first

returned.description: Number of records returned in this response

On a page carrying records, present when authorLimit cut at least one work list, naming how many and the route to the rest, or when every query term and filter value was supplied blank, so the page lists the whole index unfiltered. On any page, present when rows or authorLimit was above its per-call cap, naming the value requested and the cap applied — on an offset page with records remaining, also the offset that continues after the records returned. On an offset page where offset + rows would pass the ~10K offset ceiling, present naming the rows requested and the rows that fit and were applied, and, when records remain past the ceiling, cursor as the route to them. A page needing more than one caveat carries them all in this one string.

Other values are possible when a failure originates below the handler.

definition.name: crossref__crossref_search_journals_95edf1d8
definition.title: Search Journals
definition.description: Finds Crossref journal records by ISSN or title query. Provide issn for an exact single-journal lookup, or query for title-based search returning up to rows results. Title-query results page with offset — the nextOffset enrichment carries the value for the following page, up to offset + rows = 100000. Set include_works to true to also return a page of the matched journal's most recent works — the works deposited under any of its ISSNs, whichever one you passed; that list pages two ways, in two orders. works_offset is the simple one: newest published first, capped ten times lower at works_offset + rows = 10000. works_cursor has no ceiling and reaches the whole works list, newest registered first — ordered by the date each DOI was registered with Crossref, since Crossref does not walk a publication-date sort by cursor: pass works_cursor="*" on the first call, then chain the nextWorksCursor token from each response. The two cannot be combined, and a cursor walk always starts at the most recently registered work — it cannot resume from an offset. Returns journal metadata: title, publisher, ISSNs with their print or electronic form, subject areas, DOI counts (total, current, backfile), and per-category metadata deposit coverage — how completely the journal deposits abstracts, references, ORCIDs, funders, licenses, and similar metadata. An issn lookup also returns DOI counts by issued year.

query.description: Journal title search query, e.g. "Nature" or "Journal of Machine Learning Research"

issn.description: ISSN for exact single-journal lookup (print or electronic, with or without hyphen). Example: "1234-5678".

include_works.description: When true, also return a page of the journal's most recent works — newest published first on an offset page, newest registered first on a works_cursor walk. Requires an unambiguous journal — pass issn when a title query matches more than one. A journal with no well-formed ISSN registered has no addressable works list; the works lookup is then skipped and the notice enrichment says so.

rows.description: Maximum number of journals to return for title queries, or works when include_works is true (1–500 per call, default 10). A larger value, up to 1000, returns 500 and says so in notice; nextOffset and nextWorksOffset continue after the records returned.

offset.description: Zero-based offset into the title-query journal list. Pass the nextOffset value from the previous response to continue. Capped at offset + rows = 100000: a page that would pass it returns the journals that fit and says so in notice, and an offset at or past it is refused. Ignored when issn is set, which resolves exactly one record.

works_offset.description: Zero-based offset into the journal works list when include_works is true. Pass the nextWorksOffset value from the previous response to continue. Capped at works_offset + rows = 10000: a page that would pass it returns the works that fit and says so in notice, and a works_offset at or past it is refused; use works_cursor to read the whole list. Cannot be combined with works_cursor.

works_cursor.description: Cursor token for deep paging of the journal works list when include_works is true. Pass "*" to start the walk at the most recently registered work, then pass the nextWorksCursor value from each response. A walk runs by the date each DOI was registered with Crossref, newest first, not by publication date — Crossref does not walk a publication-date sort by cursor. Has no offset ceiling and cannot be combined with works_offset.

issnL.description: Linking ISSN (ISSN-L). Crossref journal records do not carry one, so this is normally absent; issnTypes says which ISSN is print and which electronic.

issn.description: All ISSN variants for this journal

issnTypes.description: Each ISSN with its form — print or electronic

type.description: ISSN form, e.g. "print" or "electronic". Absent when Crossref records no form for this ISSN.

totalDois.description: Total registered DOIs in this journal

currentDois.description: DOIs issued in the current window — this year and the two before it

backfileDois.description: DOIs issued before the current window

coverage.description: Per-category metadata deposit coverage for this journal — each a 0–1 fraction split into current and backfile DOIs. Signals how completely the journal deposits abstracts, references, ORCIDs, funders, licenses, and similar metadata. A window with no DOIs reports every fraction as 0, so read each fraction beside currentDois and backfileDois.

items.description: Metadata deposit coverage for one category

doisByYear.description: Registered DOIs per issued year, ascending by year; a year with no DOIs has no entry. Returned on an issn lookup only — title-query results omit it.

items.description: DOI count for one issued year
Journal record

recentWorks.description: Page of works from the matched journal, newest first — by publication date on an offset page, by Crossref registration date on a works_cursor page. Requires include_works, and absent even then when the matched journal has no well-formed registered ISSN — the works list is addressable by ISSN alone, and the notice enrichment says so.

doi.description: Work DOI

type.description: Work type

published.description: Publication date — the first of published, published-print, and published-online that names one. A component Crossref records as unknown is omitted, and so is every component below it.

journalCount.description: Number of journal records returned in this page

Absent otherwise. A page needing more than one caveat carries them all in this one string.

definition.name: crossref__crossref_search_funders_2aa21040
definition.title: Search Funders
definition.description: Finds funders registered in the Crossref Funder Registry by name or funder DOI. Provide funder_doi for an exact single-funder lookup — the full DOI ("10.13039/100000001"), the bare registry ID ("100000001"), or either behind a doi: or https://doi.org/ prefix — or query for name-based search. Name-query results page with offset — the nextOffset enrichment carries the value for the following page, up to offset + rows = 100000. Set include_works to true to also return a page of the most recent works funded by the matched funder; that list pages two ways, in two orders. works_offset is the simple one: newest published first, capped ten times lower at works_offset + rows = 10000. works_cursor has no ceiling and reaches the whole funded-works list, newest registered first — ordered by the date each DOI was registered with Crossref, since Crossref does not walk a publication-date sort by cursor: pass works_cursor="*" on the first call, then chain the nextWorksCursor token from each response. The two cannot be combined, and a cursor walk always starts at the most recently registered work — it cannot resume from an offset. This list also counts works funded by the funder's registry descendants, which a crossref_search_works filter on {"funder": "10.13039/<id>"} does not; a funder_doi lookup returns those descendants' registry IDs as descendants, and the funder's own ID OR'd with each of them in the funder filter ({"funder": "<id>,funder:<descendant>,…"}) counts the same scope with date, type, or other filters. Returns funder name, registry ID, country, and alternate names, plus the work count of the ID alone on a funder_doi lookup. The Funder Registry supersedes entries, and a deprecated one answers to the same names as its successor while carrying only a fraction of its works: such a record carries replacedBy with the superseding registry ID and the response carries a notice naming it. The replacement is never followed automatically — re-run with funder_doi set to that ID to get the current entry.

query.description: Funder name search query, e.g. "National Science Foundation" or "Wellcome Trust"

funder_doi.description: Funder DOI for exact lookup — the full DOI "10.13039/100000001" (NSF) or the bare registry ID "100000001". Supersedes query when provided.

anyOf.description: Funder registry ID or funder DOI, e.g. "100000001"

include_works.description: When true, also return a page of works funded by the matched funder. Requires an unambiguous funder — pass funder_doi when a name query matches more than one.

rows.description: Maximum funders to return for name queries, or works when include_works is true (1–1000, default 10).

offset.description: Zero-based offset into the name-query funder list. Pass the nextOffset value from the previous response to continue. Capped at offset + rows = 100000: a page that would pass it returns the funders that fit and says so in notice, and an offset at or past it is refused. Ignored when funder_doi is set, which resolves exactly one record.

works_offset.description: Zero-based offset into the funded-works list when include_works is true. Pass the nextWorksOffset value from the previous response to continue. Capped at works_offset + rows = 10000: a page that would pass it returns the works that fit and says so in notice, and a works_offset at or past it is refused; use works_cursor to read the whole list. Cannot be combined with works_cursor.

works_cursor.description: Cursor token for deep paging of the funded-works list when include_works is true. Pass "*" to start the walk at the most recently registered work, then pass the nextWorksCursor value from each response. A walk runs by the date each DOI was registered with Crossref, newest first, not by publication date — Crossref does not walk a publication-date sort by cursor. Has no offset ceiling and cannot be combined with works_offset.

id.description: Funder registry ID

country.description: Free-text place the registry records for this funder. Usually a country name, but supranational entries carry values like "European Union" — there is no machine-readable country code on the record.

worksCount.description: Works asserting this registry ID alone — the total a crossref_search_works funder filter on this ID returns, not counting the funder's registry descendants. Returned on a funder_doi lookup; name-query rows omit it.

replacedBy.description: Registry IDs that supersede this funder. Present only on a deprecated entry — a deprecated funder carries a fraction of its successor's works, so re-run with funder_doi set to one of these IDs to reach the current entry. Pass a bare ID ("501100004543") or the full DOI.

replaces.description: Registry IDs this funder supersedes. Present only when the funder has absorbed a deprecated entry; works registered against those IDs are not counted here.

descendants.description: Registry IDs of every funder below this one in the Funder Registry hierarchy, at every depth, bare as Crossref lists them ("100000054"). Present on a funder_doi lookup of a funder that has any; name-query rows never carry it. The funded-works list counts their works; to count that scope with filters, OR this funder's ID and each of these in a crossref_search_works funder filter: {"funder": "<id>,funder:<descendant>,…"}.

items.description: Funder record

fundedWorks.description: Page of works funded by the matched funder, newest first — by publication date on an offset page, by Crossref registration date on a works_cursor page. Only present when include_works is true.

doi.description: Work DOI

type.description: Work type

published.description: Publication date — the first of published, published-print, and published-online that names one. A component Crossref records as unknown is omitted, and so is every component below it.

items.description: Work summary

funderCount.description: Number of funder records returned in this page

fundersTotal.description: Total funder records matching the query in Crossref

nextOffset.description: Value to pass as offset on the next call for the following page of funders. Absent when this page ends the matches or reaches the 100000-record offset ceiling.

fundedWorksTotal.description: Total count of funded works for the matched funder, including works funded by its registry descendants, when include_works is true

nextWorksOffset.description: Value to pass as works_offset on the next call for the following page of funded works. Absent when this page ends the works list, reaches the 10000-record offset ceiling, or was requested with works_cursor.

nextWorksCursor.description: Value to pass as works_cursor on the next call for the following page of funded works. Present only on a page requested with works_cursor, and absent once the walk reaches the end of the works list.

notice.description: Guidance on a page that needs a caveat: a query nothing matched, an offset or works_offset past the end of a list that did match, a page whose offset + rows would pass one of the route offset ceilings, cut to the rows that fit (naming the rows requested and applied), a page that reaches one of those ceilings with records still unretrieved (naming the route to them), a returned funder that the Funder Registry has deprecated in favor of another entry, or a query or funder_doi supplied blank with nothing else to search by, so the page lists every funder unfiltered. Absent otherwise. A page needing more than one caveat carries them all in this one string.
